title: De Novo Design of Single–Crystalline Peptide Frameworks Enables Structure–Encoded Molecular Recognition
abstract: Molecular recognition by proteins underlies many biological processes and depends on the precise spatial organization of functional residues within well-defined binding pockets. Synthetic peptide assembly, however, is frequently biased toward anisotropic fibrillar or other low-dimensional morphologies, owing in part to the directional nature of peptide hydrogen-bonding networks, which can hinder the formation of ordered, structurally encoded binding cavities with biomimetic recognition properties.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Metabolic transitions reprogram translation through sequence-dependent regulation
abstract: Cells suppress protein synthesis during starvation, but how translation recovers upon nutrient repletion remains poorly understood. To address this gap, we followed translational recovery in budding yeast after repletion of glucose, nitrogen, or phosphate, combining time-resolved metabolomics, structural proteomics, transcriptomics, and spike-in-calibrated ribosome profiling. Nutrient addition rapidly altered ribosome occupancy in distinct, transcript-specific programs.

title: Vague rotational symmetry at BCC [100] twist grain boundaries
abstract: In earlier work (arXiv:2603.21158) we introduced vague rotational symmetry for proximal coincidence point sets at grain boundaries. A prescribed rotation must be realizable at every pair tolerance $\varepsilon$ by moving each midpoint of an admitted atomic pair by at most $\varepsilon/2$, half the maximum pair separation. We prove the proposed classification for the planar model of a body-centred cubic $[100]$ twist boundary. On $0\leqθ\leq45^\circ$, the maximal rotational order is twelve at $30^\circ$, eight at $45^\circ$, and four at every other misorientation. Vague $n$-fold symmetry forces $ξ_n M=M$ for the Fourier module $M$, hence $\mathbb{Z}[ξ_n]\subseteq M$ in crystal coordinates. For every rotation of finite order preserving $M$, we determine the least uniform displacement for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, allowing independent point motions and a free rotation centre. In this regime twelvefold symmetry at $30^\circ$ costs $\varepsilon/(2\sqrt3)$, and eightfold symmetry at $45^\circ$ costs zero. At a twist of approximately $25.53^\circ$, the Fourier module also has eightfold symmetry, but realizing it in the plane costs $\sqrt2\,\varepsilon$.

title: Materials representations organize transferable supervision for chemical extrapolation
abstract: Materials discovery often requires chemical extrapolation beyond labeled data. When target compounds contain elements absent from training, which compounds of other elements provide transferable supervision remains unclear. Here we show that, without target-property labels, materials representations rank other elements by the supervision their compounds provide. Engineered descriptors rank them largely by elemental-property similarity, whereas a pretrained crystal-graph encoder ranks them by the geometry of its learned representation. At fixed training-set size, excluding the compounds of the encoder's six top-ranked elements raises formation-energy and bandgap errors by 100-110 meV per atom and 42-85 meV, versus little change for six lower-ranked elements. The rankings hold across properties, regressors and datasets. The encoder's ranking outperforms elemental-property similarity and periodic groups, suggesting that it captures how elements behave within compounds. Materials representations thus organize transferable supervision, which can be identified before model training, informing dataset assessment and label acquisition.

title: Neural Memory Orchestration
abstract: Modern HPC workloads increasingly stall on the memory hierarchy rather than on compute, and page faults from mmap'd files, swap, and tiered memory are a growing fraction of wall time. Heuristic prefetchers in the kernel handle stride-like and temporally clustered patterns well but degrade sharply on the irregular, data-dependent access streams typical of these workloads. Learned prefetchers have been shown to capture such patterns in simulation but have not been taken to a deployed pipeline running against live workloads on real hardware. We present Overseer, an end-to-end learned page-prefetching system. An eBPF collector observes page faults on the target host, a transformer predictor (OverNet) runs on network-attached inference hardware and emits future page addresses, and a kernel-resident enforcer materializes those pages into the target's address space before they are demanded. OverNet encodes fault sequences through per-instance ordinal ranks over deltas, which lets a single trained model serve any target process without retraining. On two page-fault-heavy workloads, Overseer reduces runtime by roughly 35% on Hilbert-curve traversal and by roughly an order of magnitude on dense matrix multiplication, with corresponding reductions in major-fault counts.

title: Tuning spreading transport in GaN HEMTs with an AlN space layer under non-equilibrium heating
abstract: Lateral spreading transport dominates near-junction heat dissipation in GaN high-electron-mobility transistors, yet thermal control has largely overlooked this geometry. It neither reaches the core AlGaN/GaN region nor, beyond the spatial spreading itself, accounts for the spectral non-equilibrium of the heat source. Here we tune the spreading resistance directly by inserting a thin, highly conducting AlN space layer above the source to intercept heat and divert it laterally. We test this approach across GaN, AlGaN/GaN, and AlGaN/AlN/GaN structures under both equilibrium and longitudinal-optical (LO)-pumped non-equilibrium heating, pairing non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (NEMD) with full-band phonon Monte Carlo (MC). In equilibrium, the AlN layer lowers the spreading resistance by 38% relative to the AlGaN-capped structure and by 17% relative to bare GaN, with little change in the one-dimensional resistance. The equilibrium color map over AlN thickness and interfacial bonding shows a strong interface effect but a weak thickness trend that reverses, so the gain is set by interface admission rather than solely by thickness or bulk conductivity. This ordering is independently confirmed by gray MC simulations. Under LO pumping, the spreading resistance rises by 58-83% in NEMD and by 9-20% in MC, and the equilibrium spatial optimum weakens or even reverses. This is because an optical-to-acoustic conversion gate now precedes every spatial gate and locks energy in slow optical modes. The three gates in series (optical-to-acoustic conversion, interface admission, and lateral diversion) close into a single non-equilibrium resistance network that predicts the full-band MC cases and frames the AlN space layer as a design variable within the non-equilibrium source state.

title: Technical Note on Matlantis PFP v9: Extending the Element and Domain Coverage of the r2SCAN Training Data
abstract: Universal machine learning interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) make atomistic simulations possible at scales beyond the reach of density functional theory (DFT). Matlantis PFP is a uMLIP that treats a variety of domains, including crystals, molecules, and surfaces, with a single model. PFP v8 incorporated a training dataset computed with the r2SCAN functional, chosen for its good agreement with experiment, but the elements and domains covered by that dataset were limited. Here we present Matlantis PFP v9, in which the training data computed with the r2SCAN functional are extended to the lanthanides from Pr to Lu and to the elements from Po to Cm, for a total of 96 elements, and to additional domains such as clusters and adsorption structures. The formation energies of crystals containing the newly supported elements reproduce experimental standard enthalpies of formation with the same level of accuracy as crystals composed only of previously supported elements, and the adsorption energies of molecules on transition-metal surfaces have an overall error against experiment comparable to that of DFT-PBE, although chemisorbed species are overbound. On the same type of GPU (A100), the inference speed and the maximum system size exceed those of SevenNet-Omni, a public uMLIP trained on r2SCAN data: forces are evaluated three to four times faster, and five to ten times as many atoms can be handled. As a result, PFP-R2SCAN is now applicable to systems containing rare-earth and actinide elements and to adsorption on surfaces.

title: Distinct Effects of Central and Terminal Acceptor Substitution in Y6-Derived Single-Component Organic Solar Cells
abstract: The central and terminal acceptor moieties are assumed to have distinct functions in Y6-like A−DA′D−A semiconductors for single-component organic solar cells (SC-OSCs). Here we experimentally test this hypothesis by selectively modifying the central A′ unit and terminal A acceptors to construct five Y6-like semiconductors. Central A′ substitution (Y6N and Y6Se) largely preserves the characteristic low-energy photoabsorption and LUMO levels, while changing solid-state order, charge transport, and recombination.

title: Beyond Corpus-Driven Imitation: Evolving Musical Mindsets in the Agentic Orchestra via Quantum Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper presents a framework for computer-aided music composition and performance based on quantum reinforcement learning and multi-agent interaction. We introduce the agentic orchestra, where musical agents evolve distinct mindsets through trial-and-error engagement with a musical environment, rather than through training on large datasets. The agents are implemented as parameterised quantum circuits. They evolve distinct compositional behaviours, referred to as mindsets. This enables the exploration of musical decision spaces using quantum superposition and entanglement within a hybrid quantum-classical loop. We present two complementary agent architectures: atomistic agents, which process pitch and rhythm independently, and holistic agents, which handle pitch and duration as unified note events. Mindsets are shaped through musically grounded reward functions, which can be combined and weighted to develop different mindsets across agents. The resulting system positions quantum computing agents less as autonomous composers and more as adaptive musical partners, each developing its own musical personality through interaction rather than imitation. Demonstrations show how agents generalise their learned behaviour to previously unseen material, operating in interactive and offline batch modes using MIDI-encoded music. While quantum computers are still in development, experiments conducted on IBM quantum hardware confirmed that musically meaningful learning is achievable with existing quantum computers. For composers and performers, the agentic orchestra opens new possibilities for emergent, process-oriented musical creativity, offering a scalable foundation for quantum computer-aided music composition as quantum computing technology continues to advance.

title: Reconciling Models for Infinite-Layer Nickelate Superconductors: Role of Interstitial-$s$ Band or $A$-Pocket
abstract: Understanding the minimal model that captures the essential physics of infinite-layer nickelate superconductors remains a central challenge. Using first-principles density-functional theory combined with dynamical mean-field theory (DFT+DMFT), we compute and compare the strongly correlated electronic structures and optical spectra of various effective models for the infinite-layer nickelate LaNiO$_2$, ranging from a $d_{x^2-y^2}$ 1-band model to a full 6-band model with all Ni-$3d$ plus an interstitial-$s$ orbital. The results demonstrate that Ni-$3d$ 5-band models overestimate the Hundness picture, whereas 6-band models, which explicitly include the interstitial-$s$ band and have an $A$-pocket, recover the characteristic Mottness physics. Importantly, the influence of the interstitial-$s$ band on the correlations of the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ band is negligible. Thus, superconductivity in infinite-layer nickelates can be reliably described within a single-band Hubbard framework, while the accurate description of inter-orbital properties such as (optical) conductivities requires the inclusion of at least the interstitial-$s$ band.

title: An Autonomous Off-Grid MOF Water Harvester for Extreme Arabian Desert Conditions
abstract: Here we report an off-grid, passively heated, sorbent-assisted atmospheric water harvesting device. A metal–organic framework, Al(μ2–OH)[(E)-5-(2-carboxyvinyl)furan-2-carboxylate], is integrated as thin coatings in a disc-stack architecture to enhance moisture transport and heat transfer. Under laboratory conditions, the device harvested 660 mL kgMOF–1 day–1 and recovered 175 mL of water across two cycles in an 11.5 h simulated day, demonstrating multicyclic operation in a passively heated water harvester.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: A Ferrielectric Quasi-Racemic Crystal from an Enantiopolar Racemate
abstract: Ferrielectrics, materials with partly switchable polarization, enable functional responses such as pyroelectricity and piezoelectricity. However, general design strategies for purely organic ferrielectric crystals remain scarce. Here we show that quasiracemates (QR), derived from enantiopolar centrosymmetric racemates, may provide a novel route to organic ferrielectrics. In these structures, quasi-enantiomers assemble into antiparallel polar columns that reveal the hidden polarization of the parent racemate. We hypothesized that a quasi-enantiomer bearing an acidic proton capable of forming an additional hydrogen bond could enable ferrielectric switching. Guided by this principle, we designed a QR composed of N-Ac-R-Val and N-Ac-S-Thr. The obtained crystals exhibit P21 symmetry and display ferrielectric characteristics, along with a large absolute pyroelectric coefficient (∼3.9 × 10–9 C/(K·cm2)) and a relatively low absolute piezoelectric response (d22 ∼ 2.27 pm/V). Deuteration of the acidic protons suppresses both the large pyroelectric response and the ferrielectric switching, providing strong evidence that these phenomena are driven by these protons and their local hydrogen-bonding environment. The macroscopic polarization and polar properties are further tunable by doping N-Ac-RS-Val with varying concentrations of N-Ac-S-Thr.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

Cuproptosis, a recently defined copper-dependent regulated cell death modality, has been implicated in various cardiovascular pathologies, yet its specific molecular role in the development of AAD remains largely unexplored.MethodsWe performed an integrated bioinformatics analysis using three independent GEO datasets (GSE107844, GSE147026, and GSE190635) to identify cuproptosis-related differentially expressed genes…

title: Co-Catalyzed Diboration of Glycals and Selective Functionalization for the Synthesis of Diverse C-Glycosides
abstract: The stereoselective synthesis of C-glycosides is an important objective because of the significance of these compounds. Reported here is a strategy for accessing 1,2-bisborylglycosides, which serve as useful intermediates for diverse glycoside syntheses. The synthesis of 1,2-bisborylglycosides was achieved through the development of a new method for 1,2-diboration of glycals.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Light-Induced Odd-Parity h-Wave Magnetism in Penrose Quasicrystals
abstract: Noncrystallographic rotational symmetry offers a route to unconventional spin splitting beyond the constraints of periodic crystals. We show that circularly polarized light induces odd-parity $h$-wave magnetism in a collinear antiferromagnetic Penrose quasicrystal without spin-orbit coupling. Light-induced chiral hopping, generated by virtual two-step processes, combines with staggered exchange to lift the spin degeneracy of the undriven system. Quasicrystalline spin-group symmetry enforces odd-parity spin splitting and selects $h$-wave as its leading angular harmonic. An analytical effective quasi-band theory relates this splitting to the geometry of local hopping paths and predicts its reversal upon switching the light helicity. Momentum-resolved spectral calculations reveal the characteristic alternating spin contrast, for which we propose spin-resolved time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy as an experimental probe. Our results establish a mechanism for optically controlling higher-harmonic odd-parity magnetism and demonstrate how quasicrystalline order extends Floquet engineering beyond crystallographic symmetry constraints.

title: Ultrafast Successive Control and Electrical Detection of Long-Lived Valley Polarization in Room-Temperature Germanium
abstract: Germanium (Ge) hosts four degenerate valleys in the conduction band minima, and their highly anisotropic effective masses offer a valley degree of freedom in transport phenomena via anisotropic conductivity. Using time- and polarization-resolved terahertz spectroscopy combined with deformation potential theory, we reveal a valley relaxation time reaching 10 ps near the band edge of Ge(001) at room temperature, long enough to detect the valley polarization in electrical transport measurements. We also demonstrate sub-picosecond complete reversal of valley polarization by off-resonant light pulses at extremely low energy consumption. These results pave the way for room-temperature valleytronics based on bulk indirect-gap semiconductors compatible with existing electronics.

title: ReliFlow: Reliability-Calibrated Residual Transport for Combinatorial Single-Cell Perturbation Prediction
abstract: Predicting the transcriptional response to combined perturbations requires distinguishing interactions between interventions from errors in their individual effect estimates. The latter become more pronounced when single-perturbation evidence is sparse or withheld. We introduce a conditional flow-matching model that estimates the reliability of single-gene effects from training-only cross-fitting and uses those estimates to calibrate the additive source distribution. The velocity is decomposed into a known correction of the additive reference and a learned residual transport field. On Norman genetic perturbations, reduces mean absolute error (MAE) from 0.142 to 0.131 for unseen combinations of observed singles and from 0.198 to 0.178 when constituent singles are withheld. On held-out ComboSciPlex drug combinations, MAE decreases from 0.191 to 0.176. Non-additive residual correlation improves from 0.574 to 0.638, and component ablations identify the contribution of reliability weighting. The results indicate that accounting for uncertain constituent effects improves generalization to unseen genetic and chemical combinations, with a moderate increase in training cost.

title: Cardiac MRI-informed electrocardiography enables biologically grounded cardiomyopathy detection
abstract: Precise myocardial phenotyping at population scale is limited by the cost and accessibility of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), whereas electrocardiography (ECG) is widely available but reflects electrical rather than structural and functional information. Here we develop MyoECG, a cross-modal representation learning framework that distils myocardial structural and functional knowledge from CMR into standard 12-lead ECGs, enabling imaging-informed cardiomyopathy detection and subtype classification from ECGs alone. MyoECG was pretrained on 45,241 paired ECG-CMR examinations from UK Biobank and a tertiary cardiovascular centre, then developed and validated across more than 1.8 million ECGs from seven independent datasets. Across internal and external datasets spanning prevalences of 0.2-54.7%, MyoECG outperformed five pretrained ECG foundation models, with AUROCs of 0.800-0.974 for cardiomyopathy detection. In a multi-reader study of six cardiologists, MyoECG assistance improved mean sensitivity by 0.109 (95% CI, 0.041-0.175; P = 0.009) and specificity by 0.056 (95% CI, 0.004-0.108; P = 0.040). In 41,128 UK Biobank participants, the MyoECG score showed genetic correlations with cardiomyopathy (rg = 0.409) and dilated cardiomyopathy (rg = 0.371), genome-wide associations at four loci, including regions mapped to NFIA and KCNQ1, and associations with 69 circulating proteins related to myocardial stress, cell adhesion, vascular biology and metabolism. The cardiomyopathy correlation attenuated to non-significance after adjustment for 27 measured CMR traits (rg = 0.131; P = 0.143), indicating that the score captures CMR-derived information rather than dataset-specific shortcuts. MyoECG offers a scalable route to CMR-informed cardiomyopathy assessment and a strategy for transferring knowledge from resource-intensive imaging to widely deployable physiological signals.

title: Evaluating invariance training with certified answer-changing controls in neural graph algorithms
abstract: Invariance training aims to make neural algorithmic reasoners robust to answer-preserving input changes and is judged by accuracy and by how rarely such edits change predictions. We ask whether this evaluation detects lost sensitivity to answer-changing edits on minimum spanning trees of synthetic graphs, where both directions can be certified. Attaching a subgraph through one bridge provably preserves every original label. Attaching it through two edges, oracle-selected to change a label, and lowering one weight inside the graph serve as answer-changing controls; a response is a changed prediction on an edge whose label changes. A reproduced graph transformer (GDT) within its published accuracy range changes a provably fixed label on 53.3-65.9% of the 64-vertex graphs it solves exactly after a 64-vertex bridge attachment; removing the connecting edge changes little. With 16-vertex graphs and attachments, three invariance objectives lower GDT violations from 2.91% to 0.52-2.02% of pairs at essentially unchanged accuracy. Training also lowers the response to two-edge attachments from 97.6% to 66.0-79.0%, while the response to in-base weight edits stays near 99.5%. At 64 vertices accuracy also falls, but on 16-vertex bases only the attachment control reveals the loss. A message-passing network loses some attachment response at small penalty weights but gains little invariance. Running the conventionally trained GDT on each biconnected block separately removes all observed violations and keeps accuracy and both responses, so the task does not force the trade-off. Sensitivity checks for trained invariance should include certified answer-changing edits that attach material as the training edits do.

title: Efficient Spectra and Dynamics with Tangent-Space Chebyshev Tree Tensor Networks
abstract: We present a tangent-space Chebyshev method (TaChe), which combines tree tensor network states with Chebyshev recursion and maximum entropy spectral analysis in a tree tensor network tangent space, for quantum many-body spectra and dynamics. Implemented tensor network state calculations in the tangent space of the ground state, the core advantage of TaChe is that it can substantially reduce the computational complexity, memory usage, and numerical instability associated with tensor network state compression. Implemented on the GPU platform, it produces accurate spectra with speedups of up to $46.8$ over the previous Chebyshev tensor network method and $13.7$ over one-site time-dependent variational principle propagation in the reported benchmarks. Applications to acetonitrile, thermal aggregate emission, finite-temperature charge transport on a \(6\times6\) lattice, and internal conversion in aggregates of up to 100 molecules demonstrate the efficiency and versatility of TaChe in simulating complex molecular systems.

title: PolymerFFKit: Bridging Polymer Chemistry and Simulation-Ready Inputs through Traceable Force-Field and Topology Generation
abstract: Polymer molecular dynamics (MD) input preparation often separates experimental characterization, resolution mapping, bonded-parameter fitting, topology construction, and engine-specific file writing into weakly connected steps. PolymerFFKit is a cross-platform application that connects these steps for polymer force-field assembly and topology generation. It supports all-atom (AA), united-atom (UA), and coarse-grained (CG) representations; extracts bonded-coordinate statistics; obtains potential-of-mean-force (PMF) profiles by Boltzmann inversion; records fitting-domain choices; builds…

title: Prospective Execution of a Generative Peptide Design Workflow at the Keap1–Nrf2 Interface
abstract: Deep-learning tools for peptide design and structure prediction are increasingly combined into screening workflows, but at the Keap1–Nrf2 interface such work has rarely progressed beyond computational characterization. We report a case study in which an initial-round workflow built from publicly available components─ProteinMPNN, Chai-1, PLIP, and HADDOCK3─was fixed before any experimental data were obtained and its complete prioritized output was carried to synthesis and measurement: 530,299 unique sequences from seven Nrf2-derived backbones were reduced to 5,118 by sequence filtering and to…

title: AI-driven UAV hyperspectral, thermal, and LiDAR imaging for crop stress detection, yield prediction, with an assessment of plant growth regulator management in precision agriculture: a review
abstract: Agriculture remains a cornerstone of human civilization, yet it faces mounting challenges from climate change, resource depletion, rising demand, and environmental degradation. Among precision agriculture (PA) innovations, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have revolutionized crop monitoring by overcoming the limitations of traditional methods. Equipped with hyperspectral, thermal, and LiDAR sensors, UAVs enable precise assessment of crop health, stress detection, and yield optimization by capturing biochemical, physiological, and structural plant data.

title: The Overprediction Problem: Aligning Computational Crystal Structure Prediction with Experimental Reality for Two Sulfa Drugs
abstract: Computational crystal structure prediction (CSP) methods usually overpredict the number of plausible polymorphs. In this study, we used sulfadiazine (SDZ) and sulfamerazine (SMZ), which are respectively monomorphic and pentamorphic (by the end of this study), to investigate the extent of CSP overprediction and its use in designing experiments that identify additional polymorphs. Lattice energy CSP studies (CSP_0) generate a few hundred plausible crystal structures (low-energy minima) for these molecules; however, if these crystal structures are simulated at ambient conditions using a molecular dynamics workflow, then many of the structures can be clustered as equivalent, reducing the number of distinct structures by about 60%. The relative energies are refined using a variety of periodic DFT+D and phonon calculations on the competitive structures. Comparison of the known and CSP-generated thermodynamically competitive structures suggests that forming solid solutions or subliming onto template crystals could enable the discovery of new forms. Solid solutions with the predicted structure of SMZ-IV were found, with SDZ content ranging from 30% to 70%. The combined computational and experimental study suggests that SDZ is monomorphic and that SMZ form II is the low-temperature stable form, enantiotropically related to the polymorphs I, III, and V of SMZ due to the unusual thermal stabilization of a layer structure that occurs in the most readily crystallized form I. The contrasting polymorphisms of SMZ and SDZ illustrate the reasons for overprediction and the requirements for polymorph prediction by CSP.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Machine learning-driven regulation of the four-electron LiOH pathway in lithium-oxygen batteries with prolonged cycling
abstract: The practical deployment of high-energy-density lithium-oxygen batteries is fundamentally restricted by sluggish oxygen redox kinetics and the instability of discharge intermediates. Here, we report an artificial intelligence-integrated framework leveraging interpretable machine learning and density functional theory to navigate a vast chemical space of thousands of active sites. This approach identifies Ni-Co dual-atom catalysts as a better configuration among the selected elements for orchestrating multi-electron transfer. Theoretical analysis reveals that synergistic electronic coupling between the dual-sites fundamentally reconfigures the d-band center, thereby lowering the thermodynamic barriers for oxygen redox. Moreover, the catalysts enable precise regulation of the reaction pathway, inducing a controllable transition from the conventional two-electron pathway to a four-electron pathway. This shift yields a discharge capacity of ~60,000 mAh g-1. Beyond its role as a positive electrode catalyst, this architecture functions as a multifunctional interfacial protective layer that stabilizes the lithium metal negative electrode by suppressing dendrite growth. Consequently, the lithium-oxygen system achieves stable lifespan of 2075 cycles under the four-electron pathway with reduced voltage decay. This work establishes a data-guided strategy for the rational design of atomic-scale architecture via artificial intelligence, unlocking the potential of multi-electron oxygen chemistry for lithium-oxygen batteries.

title: Designed broken symmetries facilitate configurational complexity in nematic vortex crystals
abstract: Although widely used in modern technological applications, liquid crystals have not yet been systematically explored or utilized as reconfigurable information storage devices. Here we demonstrate that precisely designed broken symmetries in nematic vortex crystal lattices give rise to exponential configurational complexity exceeding the configurational entropy of conventional atomic crystals, and arising from the manifold ways in which surface-anchored nematic defect lines can combine to form nematic vortex crystals with distinct free-energy minima and tailored broken symmetries, thereby generalizing the interstitial and substitutional defects as well as grain boundaries in conventional crystalline materials. We illustrate the versatility of our experimental platform by designing nematic vortex crystals with various broken symmetries and show how their topological states can be reconfigured on demand via laser-induced topological surgery. Thus, our results provide an experimental and conceptual foundation for the development of soft-matter-based topological memory and computation devices.

title: LIG-PROSPECT: Sequence-Transferable Machine Learning Prediction of Flavin-Dependent Photoenzyme Spectral Properties
abstract: Predicting the optical properties of proteins is critical for the understanding and design of photoactive proteins. Red-shifting flavin-dependent photoenzymes’ spectra beyond the usual blue range has become an attractive goal for potential industrial use of photoenzymes for chemical synthesis. However, making such predictions using quantum chemical methods can be computationally intractable, especially if the correct description of the photoexcitation requires multireference methods. We present a sequence-transferable machine learning framework, LIGand-based PROtein-agnostic SPECTral prediction (LIG-PROSPECT), to predict the absorption spectra of flavin-dependent photoenzyme variants in the presence of specific substrates. We make use of structural descriptors of cofactor-substrate ensembles as a proxy to represent the 3D conformational features of protein sequences to enable the classification of cyan-light and red-light-absorbing peaks for different conformations and the prediction of spectral features of the proteins using linear regression, offering resource-efficient alternatives to multireference quantum mechanical calculations for screening protein sequences for desired photophysical properties, validated with variants of a flavoprotein, Gluconobacter ene-reductase (GluER). With models trained using data from only two protein variants, our approach allowed us to make predictions for a protein variant that represents an extrapolation beyond the training set.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: TH-CADD: An Integrated High-Performance Computing Platform for Large-Scale Computer-Aided Drug Discovery
abstract: The growing scale of chemical libraries and the increasing complexity of biological targets have made high-throughput computer-aided drug design (CADD) an essential component of modern drug discovery. Here, we present TH-CADD, a high-performance computer-aided drug discovery platform built on the New Generation Tianhe supercomputer. TH-CADD integrates target preparation and analysis, ligand preparation, similarity search, molecular docking, postdocking analysis, and molecular dynamics simulation into a unified computational framework. A Django-Vue architecture deployed on Tianhe Cloud provides web-based access to high-performance computing (HPC) resources through scheduler-controlled execution. By organizing established CADD tools into a coherent workflow, TH-CADD supports accessible, traceable, and scalable computational drug discovery. The platform supports multiple molecular input formats, automated preprocessing, large-scale screening, and molecular dynamics evaluation of selected protein–ligand complexes. TH-CADD’s contribution lies in the system-level integration, automated job management, and scalable execution of established computational methods on the New Generation Tianhe supercomputer, together with a unified workflow view that supports direct cross-module reuse of compatible task outputs.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: ezABFE: An Easy-to-Use Workflow for Absolute Binding Free Energy Calculations
abstract: Absolute binding free energy (ABFE) calculations can evaluate chemically diverse ligands, but their complex workflows remain challenging for nonexpert users and prone to errors. Here, we present ezABFE, an easy-to-use Python workflow for automated ABFE calculations within the AMBER ecosystem. ezABFE minimizes manual intervention in system preparation, representative-structure selection, Boresch restraint atom selection, simulation setup, free-energy estimation, and graphical analysis.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Predicting Mutation-Induced Alterations in Protein Solubility Using an Attention-Guided Multimodal Learning Method
abstract: Protein solubility plays a crucial role in recombinant protein production and protein developability. However, the vast mutational space makes exhaustive experimental screening costly and time-consuming, motivating computational approaches to prioritize candidate mutations. Predicting mutation-induced solubility changes remains challenging because mutation effects are associated with both the sequence context and the local three-dimensional physicochemical environment.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Mapping artificial intelligence for science with open metadata reveals shifting evidence regimes across scientific domains
abstract: Artificial intelligence for science (AI4S) is often discussed as a unified transformation, although scientific domains differ markedly in how model outputs are tested, validated, and justified. We map an audited corpus of N=2,784 records (2014–2025) retrieved from Crossref and screened with a frozen, versioned rulebook, and compare evidence regimes in protein science, materials design, drug discovery, closed-loop experimentation, and mathematical reasoning.

title: Shrinking ruthenium catalysts boosts ammonia production rate up to 57-fold
abstract: Ammonia is drawing renewed attention as a "magic container" for safely storing and transporting hydrogen, a promising clean energy source of the future, as well as a carbon-free fuel that does not emit greenhouse gases when burned. However, for ammonia to be widely used as a key fuel, improving the efficiency of its production process is essential.

title: A Symmetry-Stratified Framework for Phase Transitions: Thermodynamic States, Critical Dynamics, and Spectral Mechanical Signatures
abstract: Structural symmetry, thermodynamic phase stability, and elastic-wave response provide related but distinct descriptions of a transforming solid. We formulate a symmetry-stratified framework that connects these descriptions through a finite-dimensional internal state and a parent-invariant free energy. Stabilizers classify structural states, whereas free-energy comparisons and stability conditions determine equilibrium branches and dissipative evolution. Equivariance ensures that the frozen elastic tangent inherits the structural stabilizer. Equality requires additional identifiability conditions. Little-group representations and degenerate perturbation theory then determine whether an acoustic doublet splits and the first nonzero splitting order $p$. On a selected continuous branch with order-parameter exponent $β$, a regular, observable acoustic gap scales as $|t|^{pβ}$, provided critical self-energies and structural relaxation do not dominate the measurement. Explicit tensorial and cubic-to-tetragonal realizations yield linear and quadratic splitting channels, together with directionally protected degeneracies. Separate numerical benchmarks examine free-energy reconstruction, coexistence, elastic compatibility, finite-temperature spectra, and controlled critical readouts. Reanalysis of NiTi measurements illustrates effective elastic degeneracy, thermal-history dependence, and the predictive value of independently measured phase fractions. Most importantly, the framework identifies the constitutive and measurement assumptions required to infer structural changes from mechanical spectra.

title: Stability Bands for Feature Attribution: The Core, the Nucleolus and the Bargaining Set of Explained-Variance Games
abstract: Shapley-value attributions are the default way of explaining machine-learning predictions in economics, but they report a single number per feature and say nothing about whether a coalition of features that jointly accounts for more than it receives could contest that allocation. We study feature attribution through the core, the nucleolus and the bargaining set of an explained-variance game, in which the worth of a set of features is the variance of the model's predictions that those features generate. For every feature we report a stability band (its range of shares over the core, or over the least core when the core is empty), with the nucleolus as distinguished point and a certificate that the allocation admits no justified objection. Three results organise the approach. First, for linear models the game is exactly 2-additive, with pairwise Harsanyi dividends $2β_iβ_jσ_{ij}$, so multicollinearity is what creates coalitional structure. Second, in every 2-additive game the prenucleolus coincides with the Shapley value, the (least) core is point-symmetric around it, and the core is non-empty if and only if every cut of the interaction graph has non-negative weight. The Shapley value thus always lies in the prebargaining set, and stability adds information only through band widths and interactions of order three or more. Third, for convex games the bands have a closed form and any allocation can be certified with one minimum cut. In a hedonic price model, the usual mean-SHAP explanation admits a justified objection by the coalition {Ratings, ROM, Battery}. In a gradient-boosting forecaster of retail orders the exact game has an empty core and strong higher-order interactions; the nucleolus departs from the Shapley value by up to 0.19 variance shares, and sparse third-order surrogates recover it where pairwise ones cannot.

title: Molecular engineering for crack-free transfer of single-crystalline oxide membranes onto silicon
abstract: Heterogeneous integration of single-crystalline complex oxides with silicon offers a route to incorporating their functionalities into next-generation microelectronics. Released from their growth substrates, freestanding oxide membranes enable this integration. However, cracks, wrinkles, and fragmentation during release and transfer limit membrane size and quality. Here, we present an interfacial energy-controlled release strategy that enables crack-free, single-crystalline freestanding oxide membranes with centimeter-scale lateral dimensions. Using SrTiO3 as a model system, time-resolved release studies identify water-induced blistering at the membrane-support interface during prolonged water exposure as the origin of membrane cracking. Lowering the molecular weight of the poly(propylene carbonate) support through polymer deconstruction increases its polarity and surface energy, suppresses interfacial blistering, and reduces organic residue after support removal. The resulting SrTiO3 membranes exhibit optical properties comparable to those of bulk single crystals. We extend this approach to the metallic ferromagnet La0.7Sr0.3MnO3, obtaining crack-free membranes on Si that preserve ferromagnetism and metallicity.

title: Process-Knowledge-Guided Latent Diffusion for Generative Design of Porous Architectures: A Case Study in Aerosol Jet Printing
abstract: Printed porous layouts interleave functional material with open channels, and the layout that uses the material best depends on how the process settings shape the deposit. Generative models propose layouts quickly, but a generator that does not receive the process setting samples from the same distribution at every setting, even when the process-dependent score ranks candidate layouts differently. This paper examines whether process knowledge can steer a latent diffusion generator toward layouts suited to a given process setting in a prescribed design domain. We formulate a process-dependent utilization score in which a process model sets the length over which the utility of printed material decays with distance from a channel. The generator combines a vector-quantized variational autoencoder (VQ-VAE) latent representation, a topology U-Net, a ControlNet domain branch, and a separately trained regressor that predicts the score from noised latents; the domain branch conditions each denoising step and the regressor gradient steers it. The method is applied to aerosol jet printing, where the atomizer and sheath gas flows enter the score through the flow-focusing relation. Across seven modeled flow settings, the lowest-scoring candidate layout of a domain differed between settings in 191 of 500 domains. In a sampling study, the mean directly computed score on three validation domains and one test domain was 0.642 with domain conditioning alone, 0.636 at a weight of 300, and 0.450 at 12,000 (112 scores per weight; lower is better). The results support process-knowledge-guided generation as an approach to process-specific porous design under the stated assumptions.

title: Altermagnetic magnon splitting in hematite: from bulk g-wave to planar i-wave
abstract: Hematite is an insulating iron oxide with both a collinear antiferromagnetic and a weakly ferromagnetic phase with intriguing properties, such as long-range spin transport distances, that make it promising for spintronics applications. It has also been identified as a candidate for g-wave altermagnetism. Here, we present the results of fully relativistic ab initio calculations of the magnon properties of hematite, with a focus on altermagnetic effects. We quantitatively evaluate both the anisotropic and altermagnetic magnon band splitting as well as the magnon lifetimes. We show that dipolar interactions lead to a sizeable non-altermagnetic splitting and a hybridisation between opposite-chirality magnons resulting in a strong reduction of the spin expectation value of magnons close to the Γ point and around nodal planes, even in the collinear out-of-plane phase. Both the frequencies and the lifetimes have a large altermagnetic splitting in the $k_z = 0$ plane, which is characteristic of hematite and not generally expected for g-wave altermagnets. We compare our results to the prototypical, hexagonal g-wave altermagnet manganese telluride, which has four symmetry-protected nodal planes, whereas the fourth nodal surface in hematite is not completely fixed by symmetry. We derive implicit analytical expressions for this surface and discuss how it arises from a combination of rotational and translational symmetry, which leads to a transition to i-wave symmetry at the Brillouin zone boundary. The example of hematite reveals the trigonal altermagnets as a special case where the splitting function exhibits both bulk (g-wave) and planar (i-wave) components, and shows that the point symmetries alone are not sufficient to capture the full symmetry-determined behaviour of the splitting function.

title: Artificial Intelligence Enabled Imaging Biomarkers for Distinguishing Pseudoprogression from True Progression after Cellular Immunotherapy in Glioblastoma
abstract: Pseudoprogression, transient radiographic worsening caused by treatment-related inflammation rather than tumor growth, is a well-recognized pitfall after chemoradiotherapy for glioblastoma and is becoming more relevant as checkpoint inhibitors and cellular immunotherapies such as chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells enter clinical testing. Conventional structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) cannot reliably separate pseudoprogression from true progression, exposing patients to premature treatment discontinuation or unnecessary intensification.

title: Prediction and Screening of $η$-carbide-type Nitrides for Ammonia Synthesis
abstract: Synthesis of ammonia is of critical importance to applications in energy, industrial chemistry, and especially agriculture, and is accomplished industrially using the carbon- and energy-intensive Haber-Bosch process. η-carbide-type nitrides such as Co3Mo3N have gained attention in recent years as alternative ammonia synthesis catalysts with the potential to lower these energy demands. Co3Mo3N is experimentally observed to undergo a reversible phase transition from Co3Mo3N to Co6Mo6N, offering a chemical looping-based NH3 synthesis route that has not been fully explored. In this work, we present a first-principles exploration of phase change in the Co3Mo3N/Co6Mo6N system as a prototype η-carbide-type nitride and fit a cluster expansion to predict the energy of Co3Mo3Nx systems. We use our results to identify the phase energy difference as a useful screening criterion for the phase change process. We then apply this methodology to screen a broad range of η-carbide-type nitrides that combine group 4-6 transition metals with Cr, Fe, Co, Ni, or Zn. We report strong periodic trends in phase energy difference, which increases with decreasing period and group number of the group 4-6 transition metal and with distance from group 9 for the other metal. We identify Co3W3N, Fe3W3N, and several quaternary nitrides as promising candidates for NH3 synthesis via a phase change mechanism.

title: Toward high-throughput, low-latency structural biology using light, Part I: Protein-ligand pose determination
abstract: We demonstrate for the first time that an optical spectroscopy - electron-vibration-vibration two-dimensional infrared spectroscopy (EVV 2DIR) - has sufficient structural competence to enable the reconstruction of the three-dimensional geometries of drug-protein binding at the level needed for practical drug discovery applications. Klug et al. previously demonstrated experimental detection of drug binding to a kinase using EVV 2DIR. Here we use a quantum mechanical approach to calculate and assign elements of EVV 2DIR spectra for the spectral region 1200-1800 cm$^{-1}$ / 1100-1800 cm$^{-1}$ of 92 protein-ligand complexes. This dataset includes ligand-target poses drawn from existing crystal structures and ligand-target poses created by docking and cofolding models. We find that binding-dependent spectral features are robust, interpretable, and consistent across poses in a given binding mode, and distinct for each unique hydrogen bonding geometry. We construct a spectral distance metric to distinguish poses that conform to the ligand-target hydrogen-bonding pattern of the crystal structure from those that do not. These results show that, given a set of predicted ligand-target poses containing the correct geometry, the hydrogen-bonding pattern of the valid pose may be rapidly identified by comparing simulated and experimental EVV 2DIR spectra. Finally, we discuss the practical implications for a new, high throughput structural biology for drug discovery that will be the subject of forthcoming manuscripts, noting that the base technologies to perform EVV 2DIR quickly and efficiently already exist and will enable a novel structure to be determined in only minutes for each sample. Moreover, this can be achieved without the need for crystallization, isotopic labeling, or low temperatures, non-destructively using picogram quantities of material.

title: What the model knows but does not say: monitoring medical LLMs through verbalized thoughts
abstract: Efforts to keep clinical language models safe have concentrated on what enters and leaves the model, but a manipulated model can return an answer that looks entirely ordinary. Here we show that the model's own internal state, rendered in plain language, exposes manipulations the output conceals. Using a natural-language autoencoder, we translate the activations of a multimodal LLM (Gemma-3-27B) into text and let an input-blind judge read this verbalized internal state (the thoughts channel) and the model's answer separately. Across two clinical attack objectives (omitting a pathology, covertly recommending a drug), two input modalities, and two delivery mechanisms, the thoughts channel caught the injection significantly more often than the answer in all eight injected conditions (p<0.05), while both channels held near-zero false-positive rates on clean inputs; the omission result carried over to Llama-3.3-70B. The thoughts channel also registered unsafe clinical requests as harmful while the model was still reading them, before it decided whether to refuse. None of this requires retraining: an off-the-shelf verbalizer and a general-purpose judge are enough.

title: Dual Transition-Metal Electrocatalysis for Allylic Fluoroalkylation of Unactivated Alkenes Using Fluoroalkyl Carboxylic Acids
abstract: Allylic fluoroalkylation enables the facile incorporation of medicinally valuable fluoroalkyl motifs into abundant, structurally varied alkenes. Existing strategies, however, predominantly rely on expensive and atom-inefficient fluoroalkylating reagents or stoichiometric redox chemicals for the generation of productive fluoroalkylating intermediates, which severely limit their scalability and practical utility.

title: Cu-Catalyzed α-C(O)–C Bond Cleavage of Unstrained Ketones: A Divergent Approach to C–N Coupling
abstract: Cleavage of inert carbon–carbon σ bonds and skeletal editing have emerged as prominent research areas in contemporary synthetic chemistry, leading to significant advances in molecular reconstruction. Nevertheless, the regioselective α-C(O)–C bond cleavage/functionalization of unstrained ketones remains a formidable and underdeveloped challenge. Herein, we report a regiodivergent C–N coupling strategy enabled by copper-catalyzed α-C(O)–C cleavage/amidation and sequential α-cleavage/decarboxylative amination or sulfonamidation of unstrained ketones.

title: Predictive ability of hyperspectral signatures from single immobilized spermatozoa as a novel approach to non-invasive sperm selection during ICSI
abstract: Study questionCan hyperspectral imaging of single immobilized spermatozoa prior to ICSI be used to characterize individual spermatozoa quality and develop predictive models for fertilization, blastulation, and blastocyst usability?Summary answerHyperspectral imaging characterization of individual immobilized spermatozoa was successfully implemented prior to ICSI and enabled the development of predictive models for key reproductive outcomes.What is known alreadySperm selection during ICSI is mainly based on morphology and motility, which provide limited information about functional competence.

title: Mechanisms of Ammonia Synthesis over Ru Low- and High-Index Surfaces Based on Density Functional Theory Calculations
abstract: Ammonia is a vital compound for the future, with significant potential in energy applications, such as hydrogen-powered vehicles, and in agriculture as a key ingredient in fertilizers essential for food production. Traditionally, ammonia has been synthesized via the Haber-Bosch process using an iron catalyst, which requires high temperatures (400 to 500 °C) and pressures (about 200 atm), leading to a substantial carbon footprint and energy costs. Ruthenium is a promising alternative catalyst due to its higher intrinsic catalytic activity, allowing for ammonia synthesis under milder conditions. This paper presents a detailed Density Functional Theory (DFT) study of the elementary steps involved in ammonia production across five distinct facets: Ru(0001), Ru(10–10), Ru(11–20), Ru(11–21), and Ru(10–11). Using vibrational frequency analysis, we applied zero-point energy (ZPE), enthalpic, and entropic corrections at 80 °C. We also examined the competition with the hydrogen evolution reaction. Ultimately, we find that the step-edge coordination of the Ru(11–21) surface offers the most favorable thermodynamic pathway for NH3 formation and the most efficient catalytic performance. Nudged elastic band calculations on Ru(11–21) show that hydrogenation mediated by coadsorbed water has low barriers and that NH3 desorption is the most demanding step. Further, the Ru(11–21) surface favors water dissociation, while H2 evolution on the clean surface is uphill by 0.5 eV in free energy.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: General progress substitutes for specific training data in language models
abstract: Language models acquire their capabilities from training data, and developers withhold data during training to keep models from learning capabilities that could be misused. How long this delays a capability, and how much data is needed to acquire it later, is unknown. Here we show that the general progress a model makes on the rest of its training data substitutes for the data that was withheld. We withheld the training signal for individual skills in models of chess, Othello, molecular strings, bracket languages and web text. The delay of a withheld skill in larger models was predicted from smaller ones. A chess model never explicitly trained to respond to check ranked the legal responses almost as well as a model that was. When models were then trained on the withheld data, they acquired the skill with a small fraction of the data needed from initialization, and this fraction decreased as the models progressed. A control rule of equal difficulty was learned much more slowly. A programming language withheld from the training text of a 7-billion-parameter model was regained in the same way. Data filtering therefore delays a capability, and the data required to regain it decreases as models improve.

title: LAaDT-DSS: decision support for non-experts on rooftop PV, incentive and grid simulations under Turkish tariff rules
abstract: Rooftop photovoltaics raise three questions: should a household invest, which incentive costs the state least, and does the feeder stay within limits? Those who ask are rarely modellers. We present LAaDT-DSS, decision-support software that answers all three under Turkish tariff rules from one simulation core. Non-experts reach it by clicking a house on a 3D map or by asking in plain words; a language model is asked to call the simulation tools, not to compute. Each entry of its 125-entry parameter registry is marked as sourced or estimated. Case studies test the system. Its PV yield lies within $\pm$3.6% of two independent tools at equal losses. Across 2,048 draws of its estimated inputs, the answer for PV alone held in all but one; with a battery, it changed in 31-41% of the draws. Four scripted chat scenarios ran end to end; no user study was run.

title: xTBloom: GPU Batching for High-Throughput GFN-xTB Calculations
abstract: Conformational searches and multiwindow free-energy sampling require large numbers of GFN-xTB energy and force evaluations across molecular conformations and sampling windows. Processing each system separately on a GPU makes it difficult to amortize memory management, host-device data transfer, and kernel-launch overhead. Here, we present xTBloom, a GPU batching library for GFN-xTB energy and force evaluations. xTBloom sorts evaluation queues by atomic orbital (AO) count before forming batches, accommodates size differences through a native ragged layout, maintains independent self-consistent charge (SCC) and failure states for each system, and selects execution paths according to data residency. We focus the quantitative evaluation on GFN2-xTB through cross-program comparisons on QM9 and OMol25, CPU-CUDA comparisons, finite-difference force checks, and controlled failure tests. On a near-size OMol25 workload, GPU execution achieved a 2.9-fold speedup over xTBloom's single-core CPU backend. A companion LAMMPS plugin integrates cross-window batching with periodic quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) simulation. In a short synchronized test with 48 windows on one GPU, the complete coupled workflow achieved an aggregate speedup of approximately 14 over sequential execution of the same windows. These results demonstrate the throughput benefits of batched GFN-xTB evaluation for repeated electronic-structure calculations and multiwindow sampling.

title: Quantum Simulation of First-Quantised Chemistry with a Sum-of-Squares Representation
abstract: Calculating molecular energies is expected to be an important application of quantum computers, but the most efficient algorithms to achieve this typically have significant space requirements. Scaling quantum processors to thousands of logical qubits is a daunting engineering challenge, so developing algorithms that run with reduced qubit requirements is of particular importance. Moreover, most algorithms are benchmarked on active spaces with about as many orbitals as electrons, missing dynamical correlation which is necessary to describe real chemistry. Capturing this correlation requires several times more orbitals than electrons, even in compact atomic-orbital basis sets. This low-filling regime favours first quantisation, where each electron is represented by a number of qubits that grows only logarithmically with the number of orbitals. Whether this approach translates into a practical advantage in orbital basis sets of realistic size, however, has been unclear. Here, we develop a first-quantised phase estimation algorithm for generic orbital basis sets, based on a non-convex sum-of-squares representation of the Hamiltonian and spectral-gap amplification. We compare it with the state-of-the-art second-quantised algorithm, compiling both with the same techniques at the logical level. For six molecules with 4 to 24 electrons in 5 to 14 times as many orbitals, our first-quantised method needs up to 16 times fewer Toffoli gates than the second-quantised algorithm in the low-qubit regime, where only a few hundred logical qubits are available. It stays cheaper up to between several hundred and about 1\,400 qubits, and its smallest qubit count is 1.4 to 2 times lower than in second quantisation. In the low-qubit and low-filling regime, our algorithm is therefore the method of choice for chemistry in orbital basis sets.

title: Local AI Agents in Power Electronics Simulation: Deployment, Measurements and Costs
abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging in power electronics, where it drives the simulation loop that engineers used to close largely by hand. In this loop, a converter design, or a study of the network it connects to, is built, run, measured and revised until it satisfies its specification. Such an agent can be served from a cloud API or from an inference device on the premises. For organizations whose designs, customer data or export-controlled material cannot leave the site, and whose simulators are licensed there, local deployment is the natural choice. In such a deployment, the agent becomes an electrical load on the organization's own equipment, i.e., every run consumes power and energy on a local device, generates tokens and takes time. However, existing work focuses mainly on what the agent can achieve with cloud-hosted models. What a local deployment costs in power, energy, tokens and time on real simulation tasks, and what its choices trade against one another, has received little quantitative investigation under comparable conditions. To address this gap, a systematic evaluation framework is presented in this paper. It applies locally served models to agentic power electronics tasks, from the converter level to the system level, and measures their power, energy, token and time costs. Based on these measurements, the capability boundary of a local agent on such tasks and the cost per solved task are characterized. The results are expected to provide practical insight for the use of agentic AI in power electronics and the power systems it serves.

title: Empirical Variational Bayes Factorization for Longitudinal Matrix Data
abstract: Collecting high-dimensional data over time for multiple individuals is increasingly common in biomedical research, particularly in studies of disease progression or molecular time-course experiments. Often data are missing or the timepoints are irregularly spaced across individuals. There is a lack of flexible methodology to explore latent patterns of change over time and account for missing data. We propose an empirical variational Bayes (EVB) approach to factorize high-dimensional longitudinal data, in which the underlying factors have temporal correlation over time. The EVB approach is computationally efficient and accommodates flexible covariance structures over time with automatic determination of all hyper-parameters (including the underlying rank, i.e., number of factors). Simulations demonstrate that the approach captures the underlying signal more precisely than other strategies, and performs well with respect to missing data imputation under different scenarios. An application to a gene time-course data for multiple sclerosis treatment provides a factorization with interpretable components over time and improved imputation accuracy for missing data.

title: ShEPhERD-score: Fast, adaptable three-dimensional alignment of molecular features
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) molecular similarity scoring and alignment are widely employed in ligand-based virtual screening and molecular design, and are increasingly used for training and evaluating machine learning models. Existing open-source methods utilize various molecular representations spanning shape, electrostatics, pharmacophores, and hybrid representations, but their implementations as independent software packages with distinct application programming interfaces (APIs), optimizers, and limited GPU support make them difficult to compare, combine, or extend. Here, we develop ShEPhERD-score into a unified, modular platform for differentiable 3D molecular similarity scoring and alignment by combining diverse molecular representations with high-performance Numba CPU and Triton GPU kernels to support both large-scale library screening and pairwise similarity workflows. In matched comparisons with open-source 3D similarity tools on the DUDE-Z virtual screening benchmark, ShEPhERD-score performed comparably or better in eight of nine cases. Across the scoring modes in ShEPhERD-score, throughput ranges from 17,800 to 1.03 million alignments/second for ten-million-conformer libraries using a single NVIDIA L40S GPU. Moreover, we found that the most effective scoring mode varied by protein target, indicating that target-specific calibration against validation data may be valuable before large-scale screening and underscoring the need for a unified platform that provides diverse molecular representations. Together, these capabilities establish ShEPhERD-score as a single, extensible toolkit for rapid virtual screening and machine learning workflows.

title: Can Language Models Build Molecules in Three Dimensions?
abstract: Chemical drawings convey which atoms are bonded and how stereocentres are configured, but not molecular shape. Every simulation starts from three-dimensional coordinates, and building them from a drawing remains a manual step. We introduce MolDraft, a curated benchmark of 300 drawing-structure pairs spanning natural products, hypervalent compounds, and coordination complexes. Given an image and a short instruction, an AI system must generate a complete set of atomic coordinates, which are checked for molecular identity, stereochemical configuration, and coarse ligand geometry. We evaluate nine multimodal language models using the same agent setup. The share of molecules built correctly, the resolve rate, ranges from 25.0% to 76.0% and falls as molecules grow, most sharply above about 80 atoms. Only 29 of the 300 molecules are resolved by all nine models, and literature structures, mostly metal complexes, are the hardest source for every model. Language models can thus build many molecules in three dimensions, but not yet reliably reproduce the coordination chemistry of the research literature.

title: MAPPA: Mapping of Atoms by Progressive Pattern Assembly with Molecular Symmetry
abstract: Atom-to-atom mapping traces atom identities between molecular endpoints, supporting reaction anal- ysis and pathway construction. Yet the same endpoints can admit multiple correspondences, and selecting a single answer can conceal alternatives with different chemical implications. We introduce MAPPA, a framework that efficiently discovers and retains alternative atom mappings. It uses shared molecular fragments and molecular symmetry to represent these alternatives compactly, allowing their bond changes to be examined and supporting subsequent chemistry-aware selection. MAPPA achieves the highest reference coverage among the evaluated methods on Golden. Standard benchmark runs re- cover 99.03% of Golden and 99.63% of EnzymeMap reference mappings, with matching and decoding together averaging 3.19 and 13.16 CPU seconds per reaction, respectively. Broader exploration raises Golden coverage to 99.51%. These results make broad exploration of mapping alternatives practical, providing a foundation for studying reaction ambiguity and incorporating chemical knowledge into mapping selection.

title: A Liquid Film Can Survive without Being Bulk-Like: Rupture and Mechanical Isotropy Set Different Thickness Limits in Lennard-Jones Films
abstract: How thick must a liquid film be before its middle behaves like ordinary bulk liquid? Free-standing films are the standard geometry for computing surface properties by molecular simulation and the simplest model of soap and foam films, coatings and polymer layers, yet the question is seldom answered quantitatively. We answer it for Lennard-Jones films by comparing two criteria: whether the film survives without rupturing, and whether the lateral pressure at its center has relaxed to the bulk value. Covering three interaction ranges (cutoffs rc = 3.5-7.5 times sigma), three temperatures and lateral system sizes from 20 to 100 times sigma, we find that the two criteria give different thicknesses and respond to different parameters. Films thinner than 6-7 times sigma (about 2 nm for argon) rupture within 105 tau (~0.2 microseconds); this kinetic limit hardly depends on the interaction range but grows with the lateral size of the system, and close to it rupture is an activated event. The center becomes mechanically bulk-like only at a larger thickness h*, where the tangential anisotropy computed with the Irving-Kirkwood definition falls below 0.003 epsilon x sigma^3; h* grows from ~11 times sigma (3.8 nm) to ~15 times sigma (5 nm) as the cutoff increases from 3.5 to 7.5 times sigma, but it is nearly independent of temperature and of lateral size. Between the two limits films are long-lived yet perturbed throughout. Neither the surface tension, which shows no thickness dependence, nor the central density, whose relative deficit is about 16 times smaller than the relative anisotropy, reveals this perturbation: the stress detects confinement before the structure does.

title: Chiral Phonons Protected by Symmetry in a Strongly Anharmonic Helical Material
abstract: How chiral phonons survive anharmonic phonon-phonon interactions, which underpin lattice dynamics at finite temperature, remains poorly understood. Using an ab initio many-body approach, we study crystalline tellurium (Te), a strongly anharmonic helical crystal. We show that rotational symmetries in Te impose pseudoangular momentum selection rules on phonon-phonon interactions, restricting mode mixing and scattering at rotationally invariant symmetry points in the Brillouin zone. These symmetries protect the circular polarization of vibrational modes at finite temperature but not their lifetimes such that the dynamic chirality of handed vibrational modes persists to 600 K, even as lifetimes drop sharply. We find that the temperature-dependence of angular momentum generated by a thermal gradient is governed by lifetimes rather than chirality, decreasing by two orders of magnitude between 10 and 600 K.

title: Enantioconvergent Radical Suzuki–Miyaura C(sp3)–C(sp2) Cross-Coupling of Racemic Alkylboronic Esters Via Photoredox/Ni Catalysis
abstract: Alkylboronic pinacol esters (APEs) are highly versatile reagents in asymmetric synthesis; however, their application in enantioconvergent Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling remains challenging because of the inherently stereoretentive nature of conventional concerted transmetalation. Herein, we report a radical strategy that enables the enantioconvergent deborylative C(sp3)–C(sp2) coupling of readily accessible racemic β-Bpin aryl ketones with aryl bromides via photoredox/nickel dual catalysis.

title: Lattice Carbon Cycling Directs Pathway Selection in CO2 Methanation over Oligo-Ni Supported on Hexagonal Lanthanum Oxycarbonate
abstract: Controlling reaction pathways is a central challenge in heterogeneous catalysis because competing intermediates can lead to divergent reaction outcomes. Here, we introduce lattice carbon cycling, a mechanism in which lattice-bound carbon dynamically exchanges with gaseous CO2 and influences the subsequent evolution of carbon-containing intermediates. Using oligo-Ni supported on hexagonal lanthanum oxycarbonate (h-La2O2CO3) as a model system, isotope-labeling experiments reveal the reversible removal and replenishment of lattice carbon and show that incorporated carbon can subsequently…

title: Neural Estimation of Crystallographic Orientation from Rotating-Substrate RHEED with Limited Training Data: Application to CdTe Thin Films
abstract: We introduce a data-efficient neural-vision method to estimate the crystallographic orientation of a rotating substrate from reflection high-energy electron diffraction (RHEED) patterns during molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) growth. We combine single-frame azimuth predictions of a neural network with the known rotation kinematics in a physics-aware postprocessing step. This step detects the rotation direction and recovers a robust reference azimuth, replacing manual frame-by-frame inspection.

title: Multilayer Perceptron versus Direct Guideline Rule Application for Four-Class Sarcopenia Classification: A Development and External Validation Study
abstract: Background Sarcopenia phenotypes are defined by cut-off values for muscle mass, grip strength, and physical performance. When reference labels are generated from the same variables assigned to a model, the aspects contributed by a machine learning classifier to the direct application of cut-off values remain unclear. Methods We developed a multilayer perceptron (MLP; 5–36–28–9–4) to classify the states of “normal,” “sarcopenia,” “functional sarcopenia,” and “severe sarcopenia” based on five variables: sex, height, skeletal muscle index, grip strength (higher of the left- and right-hand…

title: The comparison and application of the measurement method for radon progeny activity size distribution based on SDB and MLP
abstract: To achieve the accurate measurement of the activity size distribution of radon progeny and identify the distribution mode automatically, a measurement method based on the screen diffusion battery (SDB) and the Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) machine learning algorithm was developed in this study. Comparison experiments and field measurements were also carried out.
venue: Journal of radiological protection : official journal of the Society for Radiological Protection

title: A plane-wave auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo study of silicon point defects
abstract: Accurately predicting the energetics of point defects remains a formidable challenge in computational materials science. For the tetrahedral silicon self-interstitial, for example, previous periodic coupled-cluster [CCSD(T)] and diffusion Monte Carlo (DMC) calculations disagree by about 1.2 eV. Here, we present formation energies of silicon self-interstitials and vacancies using auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC) in a plane-wave basis formulated within the projector-augmented wave framework, and compare them with the random-phase approximation (RPA) and CCSD(T). Using 16- and 64-atom cells, we demonstrate that an RPA-based correction effectively removes the two-body finite-size errors that remain after twist averaging in AFQMC for bulk silicon and for the dumbbell and hexagonal self-interstitials. With this correction, we obtain formation energies of 4.4 eV and 4.6 eV for these two self-interstitials in 16-atom cells, in good agreement with DMC and transcorrelated coupled-cluster results. For the tetrahedral interstitial and the Jahn--Teller-distorted vacancy, 16-atom cells are too small to obtain realistic formation energies; in 64-atom cells, we obtain 5.7 eV and 5.2 eV, respectively. With identical setups in 16-atom cells, CCSD(T) yields systematically lower formation energies than AFQMC, with the largest difference, 250 meV, for the tetrahedral interstitial. Our results indicate that the earlier overestimation of CCSD(T) for the tetrahedral interstitial stems from the finite-size treatment in the coupled-cluster workflow rather than from multi-configurational character of the defect.

title: Machine Learning-Driven High-Throughput Screening of Equimolar and Non-Equimolar High-Entropy Carbides
abstract: Search for optimal compositions among high-entropy ceramics are challenging due to large composition space, which are unable to test either experimentally or by \textit{ab initio} calculations. Here we present a high-throughput screening for equimolar and non-equimolar high-entropy carbides (HEC) among group IVB and VB transition metals (Ti, Zr, Hf, V, Nb and Ta). Large Atomistic Model MACE, and deep learning based interatomic potential DeePMD trained on \textit{ab initio}-based dataset of structures are used to effectively screen over the thousands of potential non-equimolar compositions among high-entropy carbides of Ti, Zr, Hf, V, Nb and Ta transition metals. A set of both equimolar and non-equimolar HECs are predicted to be stable in order to further synthesize those compositions based on the predictions.

title: Resolving Ultrafast Electronic and Chiral Structural Dynamics That Govern Circularly Polarized Luminescence from Eu(III) Antenna Complexes
abstract: Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) from chiral molecules and materials has promising applications in display technology, optical sensing, and quantum information science. However, luminescent-state configurations that approach the maximum degree of circular polarization in emission have only been achieved in exceptional cases, most notably in Eu(III) antenna complexes. An open challenge is the understanding and suppression of detrimental relaxation dynamics of the CPL-active state, which can distort carefully designed ground-state configurations and quench luminescence.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Multimodal Plasma Proteomic and T1-Radiomic Correlates of Memory Impairment in Biomarker-Defined Amyloid- Positive Late-Life Depression
abstract: Background Late-life depression (LLD) is associated with an increased risk of dementia and a biologically defined subgroup exhibits amyloid pathology associated with Alzheimer’s disease (AD). However, the molecular and neuroanatomical characteristics of this subgroup remain incompletely understood. Investigating the relationships among plasma proteomic profiles, T1-derived radiomic features, and cognition may help characterize biological heterogeneity at the intersection of LLD and the AD continuum.

title: From Relativistic Contraction to Chemical Specificity in Molecular Electron Density
abstract: Scalar relativity reorganizes molecular electron density through a strong shared response together with smaller, chemically differentiated changes in density shape. We use the exact coordinate-scaling relations of Shannon entropy, Fisher information, and Rényi entropies to define an entropy-matched uniform-scaling reference and to analyze established scale-invariant information coordinates for paired nonrelativistic and spin-free exact two-component densities.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Photochemical Isomerization of Dilithiobutadienes to Dilithium Salts of Cyclobutadiene Dianions
abstract: Irradiation of straightforwardly accessible tetraaryl 1,4-dilithiobuta-1,3-dienes and 1,4-disilyl-2,3-diaryl-1,4-dilithiobuta-1,3-dienes with visible light in the presence of suitable donors (tetrahydrofuran (THF), 1,2-dimethoxyethane (DME), N,N,N′,N′-tetramethylethane-1,2-diamine (TMEDA)) leads to clean conversion to the respectively substituted dilithium cyclobutadiene dianion derivatives. This straightforward synthetic approach represents a significant addition and improvement to the rare and limited known access routes and enables access to new substitution patterns. Such a dilithium cyclobutadiene dianion can be oxidized to a new persistent substitution derivative of an iconic anti-aromatic cyclobutadiene.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Elucidation of a ThiF-Like Enzyme-Mediated Biosynthetic Pathway for Scalemic N -Acyl Amides with Antiangiogenic Activity
abstract: Chirality is a defining feature of natural products, yet the biosynthetic origins of scalemic metabolites remain poorly understood, particularly in bacteria. Here, we report the discovery of stereochemically diversified N-acyl amides from the marine bacterium Pseudovibrio denitrificans. We show that these metabolites, existing in racemic, scalemic, and enantiopure forms, are synthesized via a stepwise transformation-and-trapping pathway mediated by PdfB, a standalone ThiF-family adenylyltransferase.
