venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Multimodal Biomarkers in Pancreatic Cancer: From Early Detection to Precision Therapy
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains highly lethal, with a 5-year relative survival of ∼13%. For decades, CA19-9 has been the principal clinical biomarker, but its limitations-including nonsecretion in Lewis-negative individuals, false-positive elevations with cholestasis, and inadequate sensitivity for early detection-have driven a rapidly expanding biomarker landscape.

title: Doublecortin compacts the microtubule lattice through a DC1-dependent mechanism
abstract: Doublecortin (DCX) is a microtubule-associated protein essential for neuronal migration during brain development, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying its function on the microtubule remain incompletely understood. Here we show that DCX compacts the microtubule lattice, with the DC1 domain serving as the main driver of lattice compaction. Using in vitro reconstitution, optical trapping, and molecular dynamics simulations, we demonstrate that although DCX preferentially binds compacted microtubule lattices, it can also bind expanded lattices and remodel them by inducing ~2-3 [A] compaction at interdimer interfaces. This compaction stiffens microtubules and inhibits kinesin-1 and TAT1 binding. The DC1 domain is necessary for lattice compaction, whereas DC2 is dispensable for this function. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that DC1 binding induces shearing and hinge motions that stabilize compacted conformations absent from apo tubulin, thereby reducing lattice heterogeneity. Our findings establish DCX as a bona fide microtubule remodeler and provide a molecular framework for understanding how DCX contributes to neuronal development through the control of microtubule lattice conformation.

title: Branched-chain α-keto acid metabolism is controlled by SLC25A35-mediated mitochondrial import
abstract: Liver is considered a primary site for systemic branched-chain alpha-keto acid (BCKA) oxidation due to its abundant dehydrogenase content. However, hepatocytes rely entirely on import of substrate generated elsewhere because they lack intrinsic branched-chain transaminase activity. The mechanisms governing BCKA transit into the mitochondrial matrix remain unknown. We found that mitochondrial import, rather than dehydrogenase activity, determines hepatocellular capacity for BCKA oxidation. We identified MCT1 and MCT2 as transporters required for cellular entry and SLC25A35 as the essential mitochondrial BCKA carrier. Crucially, hepatic SLC25A35 expression is low and limits the liver's contribution to systemic clearance. These findings establish the molecular machinery for BCKA transport and redefine the liver's role in BCKA homeostasis, revealing that mitochondrial transporter abundance, rather than dehydrogenase levels, dictates BCKA metabolic flux.

title: Mechanochemistry-Induced Metastable State with Thermo-Mechanical Ionic Transition in a Lithium Metal Halide
abstract: Mechanochemical synthesis is widely employed to enhance cation transport in solid-state ion conductors, yet the microscopic origin of these improvements remains poorly understood because mechanochemically generated metastable states are typically characterized only through their average crystal structures. Here, Li2ZnCl4 is used as a model halide to demonstrate that high-energy ball milling generates a hidden metastable state that retains the same average normal spinel structure as its thermally synthesized counterpart while exhibiting fundamentally different transport behavior. Synchrotron X-ray and neutron diffraction confirm that both synthesis methods yield normal spinel structured Li2ZnCl4 with space group Fd̅3m. Nevertheless, the ball-milled material undergoes a thermo-mechanically activated ionic transition between 50 and 90 °C, characterized by an increase in ionic conductivity of several orders of magnitude accompanied by a simultaneous collapse of effective thermal conductivity. Variable-temperature diffraction rules out the existence of an average structural phase transition, whereas pair distribution function analysis, Raman spectroscopy, Brillouin spectroscopy and static 7Li solid-state NMR reveal local structural complexity and anomalous lattice dynamics associated with a metastable high-conductivity state. Heating progressively relaxes this high-Li-conducting state through crystallite growth and microstructural and local structural reorganization, while externally applied pressure suppresses this relaxation and preserves reversible switching of the conductivity during repeated thermal cycles. These results demonstrate that mechanochemistry can engineer hidden metastable functional states whose transport properties are governed by coupled temperature-pressure-time dynamics rather than by changes in average crystal symmetry, and highlight the importance of studying both the average and local structure. Moreover, the study establishes Li2ZnCl4 as a model system for understanding and exploiting thermo-mechanically activated transport in metastable cation-conducting materials.

title: Parametric and AI-Assisted Design of Right-Handed Four-Helix Coiled Coils
abstract: Right-handed, antiparallel -helical coiled coils are rare in nature and remain challenging targets for de novo protein design. Here, we combined parametric backbone generation with deep-learning-based sequence design and structure prediction to systematically explore this underrepresented region of coiled-coil structural space. We compared three ProteinMPNN design strategies: repeat-constrained homotetramer design, unconstrained homotetramer design, and unconstrained heterotetramer design. Removing strict sequence repeat constraints increased the fraction of designs satisfying structural confidence and topology criteria approximately sixfold, from 0.44% to 2.80%, while simultaneous optimization of two distinct peptide sequences yielded a success rate of 3.04%. Selected designs were evaluated for assembly using a split-luciferase complementation assay in mammalian cells, followed by circular dichroism spectroscopy and molecular dynamics simulations. Five of six experimentally characterized designs exhibited predominantly -helical structures, with apparent melting temperatures ranging from 55.2 to 72.5 {degrees}C. The crystal structure of the most stable design, Heteromer-2, determined at 1.92 [A] resolution, confirmed the intended right-handed, antiparallel architecture, with a backbone RMSD of only 0.45 [A] relative to the computational model. Our findings establish a strategy for designing noncanonical coiled-coil architectures by combining precise parametric control of backbone geometry with flexible, AI-assisted sequence optimization.

title: Molecular Structure Determines Phase Selectivity in Quasi-2D Halide Perovskites
abstract: Controlling the phase distribution in quasi-two-dimensional (2D) halide perovskites (HPs) is a crucial bottleneck for bespoke manipulation of their optoelectronic functionalities. This mainly lies in the subtle interaction between molecular spacers and inorganic precursors during crystallization that steers phase synthesizability, which has been poorly explored. Here, we investigate the synthesis spaces of two distinct quasi-2D HPs incorporating phenylethylammonium (PEA) and octylammonium (OA)-possessing comparable molecular masses but different structures and chemical properties.

title: Scientists create a remarkable new rechargeable battery using vitamin B12
abstract: Scientists have found a surprising new use for vitamin B12, developing a rechargeable battery that uses the essential nutrient to help generate and store electricity. The prototype survived up to 250 charging cycles and could open the door to safer, cheaper, and more environmentally friendly alternatives to lithium-ion batteries.

title: Morphological Changes and Mechanistic Analysis in Osteoblasts Induced by Long-Term Exposure to Radioactive Strontium
abstract: Radioactive strontium-89 (89Sr) is preferentially deposited in bone tissue, where it directly interacts with osteoblasts; however, the morphological and molecular consequences of sustained 89Sr exposure remain poorly characterized. In this study, mouse pre-osteoblast MC3T3-E1 cells were induced to differentiate into osteoblasts and continuously exposed to 3.7 x 103 Bq/mL 89Sr for nine consecutive passages. Morphological alterations were monitored throughout the exposure period, and the cells were subjected to RNA transcriptomic sequencing, non-targeted GC/MS-based metabolomics, and non-targeted LC/MS-based lipidomics, followed by integrative bioinformatics analysis. Prolonged 89Srr exposure markedly enlarged the cell nuclei and increased the number of intracellular vesicles in osteoblasts. Multi-omics co-enrichment analysis revealed metabolic perturbations centered on the "choline metabolism in cancer" and "fat digestion and absorption" pathways, while upregulated genes--including Hif1a, Egfr, Pdgfb, Egf, and Pdgfd--constituted key interaction modules underlying these alterations. Collectively, these findings suggest that 89Sr toxicity may be mediated through co-enriched pathways centered on choline metabolism and lipid digestion and absorption, driven by the upregulation of hub interaction modules comprising Hif1a, Egfr, Pdgfb, Egf, and Pdgfd. This study provides novel theoretical evidence for the toxicological mechanisms of radioactive strontium.

title: ScentOR: Semantic-Only Heterogeneous Knowledge Distillation for Odorant Receptor Deorphanization
abstract: Predicting interactions between odorant ligands and odorant receptor (OR) proteins is hindered by the scarcity of experimental structures and the wide sequence divergence within the OR family. We introduce ScentOR (Semantic Chemical Encoder via Neural Transfer for Odorant Receptors), a heterogeneous knowledge distillation framework that transfers the predictive distributions of a gradient boosting (GB) teacher into a neural network (NN) student using only one-dimensional (1D) semantic representations, achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.954 and a…
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Beyond Linear Paths: Generalized Interpolation for Flow-Based Generative Modeling
abstract: Flow-based generative models learn to transform random noise into molecular conformations by following a prescribed interpolation path between the two. Straight-line (linear) interpolation is the usual choice, but it is only one of many possible paths. We compare four paths within a single affine framework, xt = tx+ {beta}tz : linear, trigonometric, spherical and a new operator-based path in which each degree of freedom follows its own schedule. Linear interpolation is a limiting case of both the operator-based and spherical paths. The operator-based path bends inside it (contracted), whereas the trigonometric and spherical paths bend outside it (expanded). We train the same Transformer velocity field with each path on a three-well potential, the mini-protein Trp-cage and the intrinsically disordered protein -synuclein. All four paths reproduce the reference distributions with comparable accuracy, but they get there differently. The trigonometric and spherical paths resolve conformational basins early and approach the reference smoothly. The operator-based path delays part of the transport, so some features stall or briefly diverge before converging sharply. An exact relation between the rate of change of the KL divergence and the alignment of the learned velocity with the score difference, together with closed-form moments of each path, explains these differences. The choice of interpolation path therefore controls how a flow model converges, not only where it ends.

title: Sila’s $1 billion deal signals momentum for silicon anodes
abstract: Despite slowing growth for electric cars, silicon anode materials are finding a niche

title: Accessing Stable Pyridinium Nanohoops with Low-Lying LUMOs by Pyridine-Directed C – H Activation
abstract: Designing stable organic molecules with tailored electronic properties is key to advancing next-generation electronic materials. Cycloparaphenylenes (CPPs) and related nanohoops have emerged as promising p-type semiconductors, yet their use as n-type materials remains limited due to inherently high-lying LUMO levels. While pyridine-containing CPPs can be alkylated to lower the LUMO, the resulting pyridinium species are often unstable and unsuitable for practical applications. In this study, we report two complementary synthetic strategies to access bridged-pyridinium[n]CPPs as stable, electron-accepting organic molecules. A bottom-up approach enables intramolecular cyclization to form the bridged architecture, confirming the stability of this new motif. To streamline access and facilitate structural diversification, we developed a second strategy employing pyridine-directed C–H activation─marking the first example of pyridine-directed C–H functionalization directly on the CPP backbone. The resulting pyridinium-functionalized nanohoops were thoroughly characterized. Electrochemical and spectroscopic studies revealed low reduction potentials (as low as −0.84 V) and red-shifted optical absorption edges for the doubly functionalized di(bridged-pyridinium)[10]CPP. Density functional theory calculations corroborate the observed trends in LUMO energies and support the utility of these molecules as electron-accepting building blocks. Together, these results establish bridged-pyridinium[n]CPPs as a new class of stable, tunable materials with potential for organic electronic applications.

title: Self-Limiting Diffusion Governs the Formation of Iridium Oxide Electrocatalysts
abstract: Noble metal oxides, such as IrO2, are benchmark electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) for green hydrogen production, yet their electrochemical performance remains highly sensitive to synthesis conditions, morphology, and crystallinity. Their formation commonly proceeds through thermal oxidation of chloride precursors that is conventionally described as a purely thermo-temporal process.

title: CDW gap collapse and Weyl state restoration in Ta2Se8I via coherent phonons: a first-principles study
abstract: Coherent phonon excitation offers a nonthermal route to control quantum phases of condensed matter. In this work, we employ first-principles calculations to investigate the phonon landscape of (TaSe 4 ) 2 I in its charge-density-wave (CDW) phase. We identify nine symmetry-preserving Raman-active modes that can suppress the Γ − Z direct gap to the meV scale and render the system globally gapless by generating Weyl nodes at generic k points. Among them, the 2.52 THz CDW amplitude mode A (18) directly weakens the Ta-chain tetramerization, approaching a transient restoration of the uniform-chain geometry, while its low frequency and relatively small, Ta-dominated displacement make it the most efficient mode. Other Raman modes, dominated by Se vibrations, require significantly larger displacements to reach the Weyl-semimetallic regime and are generally less effective than A (18) at reducing the Ta-chain tetramerization. Furthermore, among the IR-active modes considered, the low-frequency B 3 (7) mode (1.15 THz) provides the most favorable channel for nonlinear modulation of the A (18) potential. Although the coupling favors displacement toward the CDW-suppressing direction, the estimated indirect response remains far below that required for strong gap suppression. Direct excitation of A (18) therefore remains the most effective pathway to the Weyl-semimetallic regime.

title: Expanding the SEVA plasmid toolbox for tuneable control of gene expression in Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803
abstract: The use of cyanobacteria as biotechnological chasses is considered a key point in the circular economy due to their scarce growth requirements and its capacity of fixing atmospheric CO2. However, for obtaining the most of their potential, it is often necessary to count with tools that allow the modification of the genetic expression. In this work, we have characterized a molecular toolbox for reliable control of gene expression control through induction or repression in Synechocystis sp. PCC6803 using SEVA plasmids.

title: Bivalent, Copper-Mediated Amyloid-β Binding Disruptsthe Prion Protein's Neuroprotective Conformation
abstract: Emerging evidence shows that the cellular prion protein (PrPC) is a major receptor for Amyloid-{beta} (A{beta}) and that this aberrant interaction may influence the progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, the molecular basis of this interaction remains poorly understood. Both proteins strongly bind Cu2+, and we previously discovered that PrPC, A{beta}30, and Cu2+ form a ternary complex at equimolar ratios. Here, using electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy with isotopically labeled proteins, we characterize the stoichiometry, stability, and molecular interactions of this ternary complex. We show that the complex forms preferentially at substoichiometric to equimolar Cu2+ concentrations yet remains stable at high Cu2+ ratios. The formation of the ternary complex is bivalent, requiring the previously identified A{beta}-binding domain on PrPC (residues 95-110) along with mutual Cu2+ coordination to the N-terminal octapeptide repeat domain in PrPC. Line broadening observed in A{beta}30 NMR experiments identifies its negatively charged N-terminal residues and central hydrophobic core (residues 17-21) as the primary PrPC binding sites. Through histidine mutation studies, we determine A{beta}30 coordinates Cu2+ primarily through His14. Critically, the ternary complex formation displaces Cu2+ from a specific His residue on the C-terminal domain of PrPC, disrupting the neuroprotective cis interdomain interaction that otherwise regulates the toxic effector N-terminal domain. Using segmentally isotopically 15N-labeled PrPC, we show that while the cis interaction is not fully eliminated by interaction with A{beta}, it becomes a disfavored conformational state. Together, these findings demonstrate how Cu2+ reinforces the PrPC-A{beta} interaction, in turn destabilizing PrPC's neuroprotective fold, offering a molecular mechanism for A{beta} accumulation at - and potential trafficking across - the plasma membrane.

title: Coordinated remodeling of NAD⁺ metabolic networks across the lifespan of Caenorhabditis elegans
abstract: Changes in the metabolic network that sustain NAD+ during aging remain poorly understood. Analysis of steady state levels is insufficient to reveal whether biosynthetic or consumption pathways are perturbed or preserved. Here, we address this gap in understanding by integrating metabolomics, proteomics, gene-expression profiling, and stable-isotope tracing across the Caenorhabditis elegans adult lifespan. NAD abundance increases with age despite reductions in selected biosynthetic components. Tracing reveals reduced mid-adult incorporation of nicotinamide and nicotinic acid into NAD, alongside declining nicotinamide riboside abundance and loss of detectable nicotinic acid-derived labeling into this precursor. Early mitochondrial Complex I remodeling accompanies sustained changes in redox and energetic indices. Disruption of NAD-consuming or salvage enzymes reduces reproduction and lifespan, whereas precursor supplementation provides no longevity benefit under the conditions tested. Together, these findings reveal that NAD accumulation can coexist with extensive metabolic remodeling, establishing the importance of evaluating network dynamics beyond cofactor abundance.

title: ATSASfold: a web server integrating AlphaFold models with ATSAS-based SAXS analysis
abstract: Small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) is routinely used for the structural characterization of protein monomers in solution, and computational prediction methods such as AlphaFold now provide accurate atomic models for most proteins. When a predicted model and the experimental scattering curve disagree, several refinement strategies exist, but selecting the appropriate one remains difficult, particularly for users without SAXS modeling expertise. ATSASfold is a web server developed to help analyse the results of SAXS measurements on protein monomers and select appropriate refinement strategies. From a provided experimental SAXS curve, ATSASfold performs primary data analysis, gives a general assessment of macromolecules shape, size, possible aggregation state and data quality. An AlphaFold-generated model is fitted against the SAXS curve and the agreement with the experiment is evaluated. In cases where the fit shows significant discrepancies, a machine-learning classifier trained on SASBDB depositions assigns the case to one of four categories, suggesting the most relevant ATSAS-based strategy for model refinement: fixed model fitting, rigid-body modelling, normal-mode analysis or ensemble optimization. When needed, a graphical interface allows the user to adjust domains or flexible regions of the protein before submitting the structure to ATSAS online for longer fitting jobs. After the fitting is completed, ATSASfold provides a summary of the results. The workflow was tested on examples from the SASBDB open web-databank. These use cases demonstrate smooth operation of the web server and show how ATSASfold can simplify the transition from SAXS data collection to structure-based interpretation.

title: The C-terminal region of interferon-γ mediates evolutionarily tunable membrane interaction
abstract: Interferon-{gamma} (IFN-{gamma}) is a key cytokine orchestrating innate and adaptive immunity, yet the functional significance of its highly basic C-terminal region remains poorly understood. Here, we combine evolutionary, biophysical, cellular, and computational approaches to uncover the membrane-interacting properties of this region across vertebrate IFN-{gamma} orthologs. We show that the previously described conserved KRKR motif is embedded within a broader cationic region that is highly diverse in fish but progressively reduced in terrestrial tetrapods. Molecular dynamics simulations and experiments using large unilamellar vesicles reveal preferential interactions with anionic membranes. Furthermore, all tested IFN-{gamma}-derived peptides associate with U-2 OS cells, with the olive flounder-derived peptide displaying exceptionally strong cellular association and cell penetration, markedly exceeding that of the canonical cell-penetrating peptide R9. Together, our findings identify the IFN-{gamma} C-terminus as an evolutionarily diverse, membrane-interacting module with pronounced cell-penetrating properties in certain fish orthologs, revealing an unexpected functional dimension of this conserved immune protein.

title: Visually guided analysis of single cell proteomics data with SCP-Viz
abstract: Single cell proteomics (SCP) is a specialized, but expanding, field of research today. One of many challenges slowing SCP adoption is the inherent instability of the proteome and the changes that can occur before getting cells to a lab for preparation and analysis. Additionally, all current interpretation tools require experienced bioinformaticians to make the step from data to interpretation. Here, we present a visual toolkit that can accept SCP data from any instrument or common data processing algorithm. To demonstrate the capabilities of this tool we apply it to the analysis of dried digests of single human cancer cells following long room temperature storage. Remarkably, proteomic depth of the dried and stored samples analyzed is higher than the original analysis of these same digests on a similar system directly following isolation. Critically, when comparing control and drug treated cells, both the protein abundance and post-translationally modified peptides appear similar in both fresh and stored digests of these single cells. These findings are highly encouraging and, taken together, may help decrease the barriers for entry and collaboration for the field of SCP globally.

title: Sterically Controlled Conformational Gating of Rhodamine Spirolactam Switches for Super-Resolution Imaging
abstract: The reversible interconversion of rhodamines between nonfluorescent spirocyclic and fluorescent ring-open states underpins fluorogenic probes and spontaneously blinking dyes for super-resolution imaging. Existing strategies mainly tune the equilibrium between these states through electronic modification, whereas the role of conformational return in ring closure remains less explored. Here, we establish steric regulation of rhodamine spirolactams through amide N-substituents. Bulky substituents generate intramolecular repulsion with the xanthene scaffold, favoring ring opening. Crystallographic observations reveal substantial amide reorientation upon opening, suggesting increased separation between the nitrogen and meso-carbon reaction centers. We propose that substituent-dependent conformational accessibility modulates C-N bond reformation and the lifetime of the emissive state. The tert-butyl-substituted dye 1e exhibits an open-state residence time of 145 ms, despite its lower pKcycl. Calculations also indicate a lower ring-opening barrier for 1e than for less hindered 1a (1.12 vs 1.37 eV). Incorporating this design into HaloTag probes enables SIM, STED, and SMLM imaging. Importantly, N-halo-RBRB enables dual-modal SIM/SMLM imaging with a single fluorophore, integrating the rapid reconstruction of overall cellular architecture by SIM with single-molecule localization information from SMLM. This work identifies sterically modulated conformational accessibility as a design principle for engineering reversible rhodamine switches with tailored imaging capabilities.

title: Ancestral sequence reconstruction enables functional expression of archaeal thermostable tungsten-containing aldehyde:ferredoxin oxidoreductases in E. coli
abstract: Tungsten-containing enzymes offer important opportunities in industrial biocatalysis, e.g. to convert carboxylic acids into aldehydes without requiring co-substrates ATP and NADPH. These W-enzymes operate at low reduction potentials compared to the more ubiquitous Mo-enzymes, enabling unique reactions. Their application is limited by the lack of functional expression in commonly used heterologous host organisms. Here, we show that variants of Pyrococcus furiosus aldehyde:ferredoxin oxidoreductase (PfAOR) obtained using ancestral sequence reconstruction can be functionally expressed in E. coli with an activity of 0.86 U/mg towards crotonaldehyde at 60 {degrees}C, which is a 50-fold higher activity compared to the recombinant extant enzyme. The ancestral enzymes, named ThermoAOR3 and ThermoAOR4, carrying 61 and 84 mutations respectively, were purified using a single-step affinity purification, showed a kcat of 0.95 and 0.86 s-1 at 60 {degrees}C, respectively, and have Km values comparable to native PfAOR. ThermoAOR3 contained a redox active [4Fe-4S] cluster like native PfAOR. Furthermore, it contained 10-15% of the expected pterin cofactor, W and Fe, which indicates the enzyme production can still be improved. Altogether, we demonstrate the first heterologous expression of a functionally active W-AOR using a widely used bacterial host, which represents a breakthrough enabling exploration of these enzymes for industrial biocatalysis.

title: Side-Reaction Pathways and Catalyst Deactivation during ATRP of N-Vinylpyrrolidone
abstract: The atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP) of N-vinylpyrrolidone (NVP) remains challenging due to the low activation of the vinyl group and the prevalence of competing side reactions. In this work, we systematically investigated the polymerization of NVP using alkyl bromide initiators and Cu(Me6Cyclam)Br-based catalysts under a range of solvent environments and monomer concentrations.

title: The Hg + O → HgO Reaction on the Triplet Potential Energy Surface: A CCSD(T)/VTST Investigation
abstract: The gas-phase reaction of atomic mercury (Hg) with ground-state atomic oxygen (O(3P)) is relevant to mercury oxidation in combustion flue gases and non-thermal plasma environments. However, no experimental rate constants for this reaction are available in the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Chemical Kinetics Database. Here, the reaction is investigated using density functional theory at the B3LYP-D3(BJ)/SDD+6-311++G(3df,3pd) level, combined with CCSD(T) single-point energy calculations.

title: Analytic Hessian for mixed-reference spin-flip time-dependent density functional theory
abstract: Mixed-reference spin-flip time-dependent density functional theory (MRSF-TDDFT) describes diradicals and nearly degenerate states largely free of the spin contamination of spin-flip (SF) TDDFT, but its Hessian has been available only numerically. Within the Tamm–Dancoff approximation, we derive and implement the analytic Hessian of MRSF-TDDFT with restricted open-shell references, including SF-TDDFT as a special case, and the analytic polarizability derivative for excited-state Raman intensities.

title: From De Novo Molecular Design to Experimentally Validated Protein-Protein Interaction Modulators
abstract: Identifying bioactive small molecules requires balancing target affinity with physicochemical and pharmacokinetic properties compatible with drug development. This is particularly challenging in the development of small-molecule modulators of protein–protein interactions (PPIs) due to the structural complexity of protein interfaces. Here, we developed an integrated workflow combining de novo molecular design with similarity-guided identification of existing compounds from public chemical libraries.

title: Digital twin reconstruction of red blood cell aging using Raman chemometrics and systems modeling
abstract: Red blood cell (RBC) storage aging involves progressive metabolic and oxidative alterations that compromise membrane integrity and transfusion quality. However, conventional endpoint measurements provide limited information on individual aging dynamics and their predictability. This study presents an experimentally constrained digital twin framework integrating Raman spectral analysis, chemometric modeling, and mechanistic simulation to reconstruct RBC aging trajectories and predict donor-specific hemolysis.

title: Programmable Nanofluidic Confinement: From Static Nanotopographies to Reversible Electrokinetic Trapping
abstract: Single-molecule analysis increasingly relies on the ability to immobilize, confine, and manipulate biomolecules in solution. Nanofluidic devices provide a powerful route to this goal by using embedded nanotopographies on-chip to define free-energy landscapes that enable spatial manipulation, transport, confinement, and conformations that can be leveraged for biomedical applications. One classic example for molecular confinement is DNA extension in nanochannels, which has allowed for high-throughput genomic sequencing on-chip.

title: Understanding a Helix Reverse Path in Perfluoroalkanes from a Neural Network Potential
abstract: The helical handedness of perfluoroalkanes and polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) is considered to reverse through localized helix-reversal defects. Earlier studies with empirical and semiempirical potentials described how such defects form and move. The helix, however, originates from hyperconjugation, and the reversal pathway of a single molecule has not yet been examined with a potential that includes this quantum-chemical effect.

title: Drug-resistance phenotypes in FGFR deep mutational scanning are carried by a single-residue positional statistic that transfers across FGFR1–3 and weakens in FGFR4
abstract: Motivation: Drug-resistance mutations are a clinically central but poorly predicted phenotype: pathogenicity predictors trained on disease labels misrank them, and our recent benchmark of five static predictor families (AlphaMissense, FoldX stability, FoldX interaction energy, ThermoMPNN-D and AutoDock Vina) showed that biophysical scores predict FGFR resistance poorly. Whether supervised recalibration on functional deep mutational scanning (DMS) labels can repair this, and what feature class carries the signal, remains untested.

title: 6,7-Difunctionalized 2-Azanorbornanes from a Bench-Stable Aziridinium Salt: Scope, Limitations, and Multigram Synthesis
abstract: 2-Azanorbornanes (2-azabicyclo[2.2.1]heptanes) are present in approved drugs, yet practical methods for their functionalization at C6 and C7 are scarce. Herein, we report a two-cycle approach to 6,7difunctionalized 2-azanorbornanes from a single aziridinium salt. The salt is prepared in two steps from cyclopentadiene on a scale of up to 300 g per run. It is a bench-stable crystalline solid that can be stored and handled as a regular reagent. In the first cycle, O-, N-, S-, F-, C-, and P-nucleophiles open the aziridinium ring at C6 with complete regio- and stereoselectivity.

title: Surface Oxide Instability Exposes Metallic Pd as the Active Phase for Electrochemical Nitrogen Oxidation
abstract: The electrocatalytic nitrogen oxidation reaction (NOR) offers a potential route for sustainable N 2 conversion into valuable nitrogen-containing products. Pd-based electrocatalysts show promising NOR selectivity, but it remains unclear whether this selectivity arises from metallic Pd or from the surface oxide formed under anodic conditions. Here, we investigate NOR and the competing oxygen evolution reaction (OER) on a PdO 2 /Pd system representing a partially oxidized Pd electrode, using density functional theory and the computational hydrogen electrode approach.

title: Chemical Filtering of Thymine over Uracil by Differential Hydrolysis under Dark Alkaline Hydrothermal-Vent Conditions: A Mass-Consistent, Control-Restrained Simulation Framework (UPDSF v6.7.0)
abstract: A central question in prebiotic chemistry is why modern DNA contains thymine (5-methyluracil) rather than uracil. Most proposed answers invoke surface UV photochemistry, yet alkaline hydrothermal vents—a leading candidate cradle for prebiotic synthesis—are dark environments. Here we present UPDSF v6.7.0, a mass-consistent, kinetically-consistent, provenance-tracked simulation framework that tests whether differential hydrolysis stability alone can chemically filter thymine over uracil in dark, alkaline, high-temperature conditions.

title: Ionic routers encode GPCR activation state on both sides of the membrane
abstract: In both class A and B1 G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), certain charged residues exchange one salt-bridge partner for another between the active and inactive states: each binds one oppositely charged residue in the active state and a different one in the inactive state, with neither partner bound in both. Their ionic bonds are rerouted rather than lost, and neither state leaves them free. Such residues are called ionic routers [1].

title: Desolvation-Based Encapsulation of Nanoparticles in Protein Nanocarriers: From Multilabel Nanocomposites to Biosensing Reagents
abstract: Effective surface functionalization is a key requirement for the application of nanoparticles in biomedicine. Protein-based coatings offer a versatile solution, providing abundant functional groups, colloidal stabilization, and a well-established basis for bioconjugation. This review examines desolvation as a method for encapsulating nanoparticles within covalently cross-linked protein matrices, yielding nanocomposites that can contain multiple nanoparticles within a single protein carrier.

title: Optimization and Microstructural Analysis of Underwater Friction Stir Welding of AA6063 Aluminum Alloy
abstract: Currently, there is a significant demand for lightweight materials, such as aluminum (Al) alloys, in the aviation, aerospace, marine, and automotive sectors. However, manufacturing industries face significant challenges in producing a defect-free joint between these metals. Al alloys are used extensively in the manufacturing sector to meet the varying demands of customers and traders. This is primarily due to exceptional characteristics such as reduced weight, corrosion resistance, and improved mechanical properties.

title: Finite-Depth Response Selection of Higher Excitations in Correlated Wave-Function Methods
abstract: We introduce finite-depth response selection (FDRS), a non-iterative finite-depth framework for constructing higher-excitation spaces, with a universal formulation across wave-function ansätz and excitation ranks. Starting from a converged lower-rank solution, FDRS propagates the preconditioned response of the omitted space for a prescribed depth and constructs the retained higher-excitation space in a single selection step, without iterative reselection.

title: Subspace Fokker–Planck Transformer: An Ensemble-Based Framework for Accelerated Free-Energy Sampling
abstract: Rare transitions between metastable states limit the convergence of molecular free-energy calculations. Here, we introduce the subspace Fokker–Planck Transformer (sFPT), an ensemble-based enhancedsampling method that transports the instantaneous replica distribution in a selected collective-variable (CV) subspace. sFPT estimates the score of the evolving CV distribution using a kernel representation of the replica ensemble, maps the resulting entropy force to atomic coordinates through the CV Jacobian, and incorporates this force into underdamped Langevin dynamics.

title: Fluorination-Enabled Stereochemical Editing of Sialic Acid
abstract: Sialic acids trace the evolutionary arc of contemporary glycoscience and continue to provide inspiration for drug discovery. However, harnessing the potential of sialic acids in a therapeutic context is contingent on unlocking chemical space and devising strategies that allow the venerable C9 framework to be selectively modified in an operationally simple manner. Enabled by judicious C(sp3)-F installation at C3, the configuration of this center can serve as a lever to facilitate a series of structural editing events in a programmable fashion.

title: High Li+ Transference Number of a Novel Fluorine-Free Lithium Salt in Carbonate Electrolyte: DFT and Molecular Dynamics Insights into Dilithium 2,5-Dioxopiperazine-1,4-Disulfonate (LiDPSO)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are increasingly constrained by the drawbacks of fluorinecontaining commercial lithium salts, including hydrolysis hazards and the environmental burden of fluorinated species. Developing fluorine-free lithium salts with a high Li+ transference number tLi may offer a route to avoid fluoride-derived hazards, mitigate concentration polarization, and potentially lower lithium dendrite risks in applicable cell systems.

title: Programming Polymer Lifecycle through Catalyst-Free Photodepolymerization and Value-Added Upcycling
abstract: The durability and functional versatility of polymeric materials underpin their widespread use, yet also contribute to persistent plastic waste and the formation of micro/nanoplastics throughout the polymer lifecycle. Developing polymer systems that reconcile functional performance with controlled depolymerization and value-added upcycling remains a major challenge. Here, we demonstrated a functional polymer platform with intrinsic photooxidative cleavage by repurposing conjugated carbon-carbon double bonds as programmed cleavage sites within polymer backbones.

title: Rate Theory of Modulated Steps: Mass Action and Fractional Orders from Thermal and Strong Coupling
abstract: Transition-state theory describes an elementary step in which one complex changes. In many catalytic steps, a second complex, the modulator, such as a proton, an electron or an ion, is bound on one side only. We derive the rate law of this modulated step in chemical potentials. If the modulator moves like the atoms of the complex (thermal coupling), its amount enters by mass action. If it binds and releases faster than the complex changes (strong coupling), its amount acts as an energy, with fractional orders. Electrocatalysis treats the electron in this way.

title: Incorporating Dynamic Correlation into Grouped-Bath Configuration Interaction with Pair-Density Functional Theory
abstract: We incorporate dynamic correlation into grouped-bath configuration interaction (GBCI) using pair-density functional theory (PDFT). Computing the on-top pair density of GBCI with the conventional cumulant-based scheme requires substantial computational time and memory. We overcome this bottleneck by computing the on-top pair density directly using exact factorization.

title: AIMETRY: GEOMETRY-SENSITIVE 3D MOLECULAR REPRESENTATIONS FROM QUANTUM MECHANICAL LEARNED FEATURES
abstract: Quantifying molecular similarity depends on both chemical composition and 3D structure, which are difficult to capture in a single fixed-length representation. Contrastive learning is a common machine learning approach to generate such representations (molecular embeddings), pulling each molecule toward a positive anchor of itself. These anchors typically come from graph augmentations that alter chemical identity or from other conformers of the same molecule.

title: Cross-Facility Materials Discovery Platform: Integrating Heterogeneous Data and Automated Experimental Pipelines into High-Throughput Workflows
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven materials discovery depends on the availability of large, highly annotated experimental datasets. However, data generated in typical materials science projects are fragmented across heterogeneous instruments, laboratories, and user facilities, each with its own formats, schedules, and degree of curation. In addition, manual sample preparation, time-consuming characterization, and changing sample form factors and holders between process steps often limit throughput and therefore dataset size.

title: Temporal Rate-Shaping in Generic Reaction and Mediator-Regeneration Networks
abstract: This study examines whether generating a consumed reactant during operation can redistribute reaction throughput over a finite observation period when compared with a batch system containing the same initial reactant-equivalent inventory. Two mathematical models are developed. Model 1 is an abstract six-species reaction network in which a bimolecular primary reaction consumes A and B while a first-order auxiliary process converts precursor X into B and Y .

title: GPU acceleration of first-principles X-ray absorption spectra: an OpenACC port of XSpectra in Quantum ESPRESSO
abstract: XSpectra, the X-ray absorption module of Quantum ESPRESSO, computes K- and L-edge spectra from a Lanczos (Haydock) recursion on the self-consistent Kohn–Sham Hamiltonian of a supercell containing a core hole. In supercell calculations the recursion dominates the cost, but XSpectra had no GPU implementation, and in the GPU-enabled versions of Quantum ESPRESSO it stopped as soon as it applied the Hamiltonian. We present an OpenACC port of XSpectra for ultrasoft and projectoraugmented-wave (PAW) pseudopotentials, validated here with PAW datasets.

title: Highly active supported nickel phosphide catalyst for the semi-hydrogenation of complex, densely functionalized alkynes
abstract: Despite the outstanding performance achieved with a variety of heterogeneous semi-hydrogenation catalysts, the classic Lindlar catalyst (Pd(Pb)/CaCO3) remains the go-to choice for fine chemical synthesis due to the large substrate scope and functional group compatibility that has been repeatedly demonstrated for it. The development of highly active and chemoselective semi-hydrogenation catalysts that can not only tackle model alkynes, but complex substrates is thus crucial for a transition to lead-free, and ideally also noble-metal-free catalysts.

title: MD-SOP: Sequence-based prediction of protein backbone order parameters across computational label sources
abstract: Experimental data for protein backbone N–H order parameters () are limited, which restricts model training and testing. MD-SOP was developed to predict these parameters from protein sequences using labels calculated from molecular dynamics (MD) simulations in ATLAS and pseudo-labels generated by S-OPPE. ESM-C embeddings and hidden Markov model profiles were used as inputs to a bidirectional long short-term memory network. MD-only, S-OPPE-only, and mixed training were compared using two regression heads. The two datasets were split jointly by sequence similarity.

title: N-Alkyl Cyanopyridinium Salts as Modular N-Terminal Cysteine Warheads for Site-Specific Bioconjugation and Living Cell Engineering
abstract: Site-specific protein modification is central to chemical biology and to therapeutic development. Stringent control over a single site delivers homogeneous conjugates and underpins the synthetic engineering of proteins and cells, which demands streamlined and reliable chemistry. An N-terminal cysteine (NCys) represents a unique canonical amino acid handle easily incorporated into peptides, proteins, and cells, yet its use remains underexplored.

title: Tracking Local Proton Activity during Hydrogen Oxidation in Nonaqueous Electrolytes
abstract: Electrochemical N 2 and CO 2 reduction in organic electrolytes containing proton donors offer promising routes for the electrosynthesis of ammonia and CO 2 -derived hydrogenated products. Hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR) at the anode offers a highly attractive anodic counter reaction. Proton activity controls each of these reactions selectivity and efficiency, yet its evolution near the electrode under operating conditions is ill defined. Here, we present a rotating ring disk electrode (RRDE) method for tracking local proton activity during HOR.

title: FOdorant conformational ensembles encode topology, molecular size and polar-surface coherence, not shape
abstract: Odor is widely modelled as three-dimensional shape recognition: a flexible odorant presents a 300 K conformer ensemble to a receptor repertoire, implying that perceptual breadth peaks at an intermediate number of accessible shapes and that explicit 3D representations outperform 2D molecular graphs. We test both predictions under a cryptographically pre-registered plan across catalogue profiles (n = 4,808), human psychophysics (n = 304) and heterologous receptor arrays (n = 294).

title: Pairwise learning of cyclic peptide membrane permeability on a matched-molecular-pair graph
abstract: Cyclic peptides are a promising drug scaffold that can target proteins considered undruggable by small molecules, but their poor membrane permeability limits further application. Deep learning has been used to lower the wet-lab burden of finding cell-permeable peptides. Most existing models are trained on measurements curated from many publications and predict a single peptide’s permeability directly.

title: Recipes for a Broad, Low-Barrier AI Bootcamp in Chemistry
abstract: Artificial intelligence literacy is becoming an important component of chemical education and workforce preparation as AI transforms chemical research and professional practice. In the late summer of 2026, we organized a 30-hour AI bootcamp for the incoming graduate students in chemistry, biochemistry, and the broader community. Here, we discuss the main goals and design principles of the event and summarize several teaching modules that can be combined to design AI bootcamps of different lengths and scopes.

title: Sustained Radiopacity of Biodegradable Iodinated Polyether Blends for Tracking Long-Term Degradation in Medical Devices
abstract: Longitudinal monitoring of biomedical devices is emerging as the next phase of personalized medicine, enabling individualized treatment plans based on radiological evaluation of devices over time. However, incorporation of a contrast agent is necessary to functionalize polymeric devices for imaging, but must be balanced by changes in device properties and biocompatibility.

title: Using potential derivatives to reduce the cost of rectangular collocation: a general and versatile approach for computational vibrational spectroscopy without a potential energy surface
abstract: We modify the exact Cartesian kinetic energy operator, rectangular collocation approach of Manzhos and Carrington [J. Chem. Phys. 145 (2016) 224110] by using information contained in potential derivatives to decrease the number of required potential points. We show that this makes it possible to substantially reduce the number of collocation points, which is important, in particular, when energies are computed directly ab initio. Vibrational band intensities are also computed.

title: UEFCCS: A Multimodal Deep Learning Framework with Fine-Tuned 3D Molecular Representations for Collision Cross Section Prediction
abstract: Collision cross section (CCS), derived from ion mobility spectrometry, provides a valuable reference for analyte identification. Achieving high predictive accuracy and effective extrapolation to structurally dissimilar molecules, however, remains challenging for existing machine-learning models. Here, we present UEFCCS, a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates molecular formula encoding and fingerprints with CCS-adapted three-dimensional (3D) molecular representations, obtained by fine-tuning a pretrained Transformer encoder using only [M+H]+ CCS data from the training set.

title: Halochromic response of a prickly pear fruit ( Opuntia ficus-indica ) extract in solution and in gelatin films: an exploratory study
abstract: Smart packaging uses natural pigments that change color depending on pH. An extract was obtained from prickly pears of Opuntia ficus-indica using MeOH:H 2 O 1:4, and its visible spectrum (400–700 nm) was evaluated in Britton–Robinson buffer solutions with nominal pH values ranging from 2 to 12. In the visible spectrum, absorption bands were observed at 534-536 nm, with stable absorbance (A 535 = 0.257-0.259) between pH 4 and 7, a bathochromic shift to 542-548 nm accompanied by a decrease in intensity at pH 9-11, and an almost complete loss of the band at pH 12.

title: Light-Induced Synthesis of Ultra Thick Polymer Brush Coatings with Boosted Antifogging Properties
abstract: Polymer brushes with thicknesses exceeding 500 nm are synthetically challenging and rarely reported, while their applications remain largely unexplored. A range of applications, including catalytic, antifriction, and antifogging/antifreezing surfaces, could greatly benefit from their highly packed and extended conformation. Very recently, ultra-thick (200–3000 nm) polymer brushes have been demonstrated with largely improved wear bearing in antifriction tests.

title: Zincrius-8: An Automated Multi-Position Flow Reactor for the On-Demand Generation of Organozinc Reagents and Their Direct Use in Negishi Coupling
abstract: Among common carbon nucleophiles, organozinc reagents are notable for tolerating esters, nitriles, Bocprotected amines, and other sensitive groups in C-C bond-formation reactions. However, few are sold commercially, and their solutions degrade on storage. Herein, we report Zincrius-8, an automated flow reactor that converts a packed bed of commercial granular zinc into an on-demand source of organozinc solutions. Using a unified protocol that does not require LiCl or other additives, primary and secondary alkyl iodides afford the corresponding reagents in DMA in over 90% yield.

title: Feedback-regulation between imination reactions and coacervation
abstract: Herein, we investigate the feedback-regulation between imination reactions and coacervate phase formation. Partial imination of long-chain polylysine rapidly generates micrometre-sized coacervate droplets, whereas the corresponding reaction with a monomeric lysine model remains strongly disfavored. Subtle changes in the structure and charge distribution of anionic aldehydes determine whether the reaction produces soluble species, liquid coacervates or solid-like aggregates. Remarkably, the formation of the condensed phase produces a ca.

title: Accelerating Adsorption-Site Screening on Forsterite with Foundation Potentials
abstract: The binding energies (BEs) of molecules on ice-free silicate grains determine their release in the inner regions of protoplanetary discs, but their distributions over adsorption sites are too costly to obtain with density functional theory (DFT) alone. Here, we assess eight foundation potentials as released, i.e. without further training, against dispersion-corrected DFT (PBE-D3) for the screening of adsorption sites on forsterite (Mg 2 SiO 4 ) surfaces, and find that their errors on reference BEs, of 6.7 kJ mol −1 or more, are in large part an offset for each molecule.

title: CARBONYLATION AS A STRATEGIC TOOL: Pd-CATALYZED ACCESS TO (HETERO)ARYLACETIC ACID DERIVATIVES FROM BENZYL-TYPE HALIDES
abstract: Carbonylation of benzyl-type halides offers a one-step route to otherwise difficult-to-access (hetero)arylacetic acid derivatives, but competing reactions and substrate-dependent reactivity substantially limit the applicability of this approach. In this work, we examined possible outcomes across a broad preparative series using a Pd-dppf catalyst system, with multiple examples exceeding 100 g. The study reports successful ester formation alongside methyl ether formation, incomplete conversion, and decomposition across diverse heterocyclic frameworks.

title: How Multiconfigurational Is Zeaxanthin? A Natural Orbital Functional Study of Its Ground and Excited States
abstract: The electronic structure of zeaxanthin presents an important challenge for understanding the relationship between electron correlation, multiconfigurational character, and optical excitations in conjugated systems. In this work, we investigate its ground and excited states using natural orbital functional (NOF) theory combined with the extended random phase approximation (ERPA). Our results reveal that the apparent multiconfigurational character of the ground state depends strongly on the treatment of electron correlation.

title: Buffer Ionization as the Dominant Source of Redox Entropy in Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer
abstract: Proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) underpins a wide range of energy conversion technologies, from artificial photosynthesis to electrocatalytic fuel production. In thermoelectrochemical cells (thermocells), PCET-active transition metal complexes can give large temperature coefficients ( α ) by leveraging the substantial entropy changes associated with simultaneous electron and proton transfers. However, the fundamental origin of this entropy change and how it is modulated by the electrolyte environment remain elusive.

title: Virtual Intact Block Extraction: Reconstruction of Molecular Assemblies across Periodic Boundaries
abstract: Reconstructing molecular assemblies across periodic boundaries requires accurate periodic placement in general triclinic cells and a criterion for whether a stored frame uniquely defines a finite assembly. Existing tools return one arrangement per frame without indicating whether contacts fix it, and voxel-based or multistep workflows can split contacting subunits in tilted cells or depend on coordinate origin and cell basis.

title: Hybrid Physics-Informed and Data-Driven State-of-Charge Estimation for Lithium-Ion Batteries Under Varying Temperature: A Simulation-Based Study
abstract: Accurate state-of-charge (SOC) estimation is central to battery management, yet equivalent-circuit filters degrade when operating conditions drift from those at which they were parameterized, while purely data-driven estimators can fail outside their training envelope. This study compares five SOC estimators on a simulated lithium-ion cell with a richer ground-truth model than any estimator uses (two RC branches, hysteresis, temperature-dependent resistance and capacity, self-heating, and sensor bias and noise): Coulomb counting, an extended Kalman filter (EKF) with parameters identified at…

title: Hypothalamic volume and cell-type changes in ageing and Alzheimer's disease
abstract: Alterations in metabolism, stress response, sleep, circadian rhythms and neuroendocrine processes are key features of ageing and neurodegeneration1,2. These fundamental processes are regulated by the hypothalamus, yet how its functionally distinct subregions and cell types change during human ageing and Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains largely unexplored. Here we present HypoAD, an atlas of the human hypothalamus in ageing and AD, including high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging from 458 individuals and single-nucleus RNA sequencing of 614,403 nuclei from young participants, patients with…

title: BALLROOM A and S–A Benchmark Created Automatically from Structurally Resolved Pockets with Homogeneously Measured Affinities/Series
abstract: Computational methods for virtual screening and lead optimization are benchmarked on specifically designed data sets to predict compound potency. Here we present a workflow and two resulting new benchmark data sets, BALLROOM A and BALLROOM S, from combining PDB and ChEMBL data. Due to high data quality standards, the formation of molecule pairs measured under the same conditions only, and avoiding pairs with close to equal potency, we achieve a reliable data collection for physics-based bioactivity prediction based on protein–ligand complex structures. When testing state-of-the-art scoring functions for docking, no classical method statistically outperforms a simple molecular-weight-based prediction, consistent with previous studies such as D3R. While challenging for physics-based methods, the prediction task can be easily addressed by simple nearest-neigbor scorers showing that the benchmark cannot be used for machine learing based scoring functions due to significant train-test inference.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Atomic-Scale Mechanisms of Sequential Phase Transformation in Hydrogen-Driven Iron Oxide Reduction
abstract: Hydrogen-based direct reduction of iron oxides provides a carbon-free pathway to sustainable steelmaking, yet the atomistic mechanisms governing sequential reduction remain unresolved. Using in situ environmental transmission electron microscopy and density functional theory, we visualize the H2-driven reduction cascade from α-Fe2O3 through Fe3O4 to FeO at atomic resolution. The α-Fe2O3 → Fe3O4 transformation initiates at the surface and proceeds through inward migration of the α-Fe2O3/Fe3O4 interface, with no detectable Fe3O4 nucleation in the examined α-Fe2O3 interiors. The subsequent Fe3O4 → FeO transformation exhibits boundary-dependent behavior: FeO nucleates at defect-rich regions of the examined high-angle grain boundaries, whereas nanovoids form within the surrounding Fe3O4 bulk in association with low-angle boundaries. This contrast suggests that local defect structures influence local oxygen-vacancy accumulation and the competition between boundary FeO nucleation and bulk void formation. Atomistic calculations further show that interstitial hydrogen lowers oxygen-vacancy formation and migration barriers and promotes vacancy association. These results reveal how local crystallographic defects and interstitial hydrogen influence sequential iron oxide reduction through their effects on oxygen-vacancy formation, migration, and association.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Environment-adaptive molecular neural networks enabled by heterogeneous threshold DNA neuron
abstract: Molecular neural networks enable autonomous information processing in biochemical environments, yet most existing DNA-based implementations operate with fixed connectivity after assembly, limiting their ability to adapt network topology to changing environments. Here, we report an environment-adaptive molecular neural network enabled by DNA neurons with sequence-programmed, heterogeneous activation thresholds. These neurons incorporate triplex-based proton-gated DNA switches with tunable pH-response windows, which regulate the accessibility of toehold and recognition domains to switch pre-encoded weighted connections between inactive and signal-propagating states, thereby reconfiguring network connectivity without changing molecular composition. We demonstrate this principle in a DNA neural network that processes 64-bit inputs, where environmental acidification activates dormant neurons and reconfigures the computational topology from a sparse convolutional neural network for coarse two-class categorization into a fully connected neural network for fine-grained discrimination among four distinct patterns. Our results establish DNA-based neural circuits capable of adapting their computational architecture to environmental cues, offering a framework for molecular information processing in fluctuating biochemical environments.

title: Daphniphyllum macropodum genome assembly and multiplexed screening unveils alkaloid modifying enzymes
abstract: Daphniphyllum macropodum, a small shrub or tree native to East Asia, produces bioactive polycyclic alkaloids of remarkable complexity and variety, making them long-standing, attractive targets for chemical synthesis. However, the biosynthetic origins of Daphniphyllum alkaloids remain unknown, and no pathway-associated enzymes have been identified to date. Here, we report the chromosome-level genome assembly of D. macropodum, representing the first genome assembly for the Daphniphyllaceae, a family in the Saxifragales woody clade. To discover alkaloid-modifying enzymes, we developed a highly combinatorial, multiplexed screening approach which enabled testing multiple enzyme candidates with multiple substrates in a single reaction. Deconvolution and characterisation identified two cytochrome P450 enzymes that catalyse the hydroxylation of the yuzurimine-type alkaloid daphhimalenine B. Specifically, CYP82C230 functions as a daphhimalenine B 2-hydroxylase to yield the natural product yuzurimine C, whereas its paralog, CYP82C231, acts as a daphhimalenine B 13-hydroxylase generating a novel alkaloid we have named yuzurimine F. These are the first reports of an enzymatic modification of a Daphniphyllum alkaloid. Collectively, this work advances our understanding of D. macropodum biology and represents the first steps towards elucidating the complex Daphniphyllum alkaloid biosynthetic pathway.

title: Wilson disease mechanisms manipulate ATP7B activity
abstract: Copper is an essential cofactor for enzymes involved in diverse processes including mitochondrial respiration and the metabolism of neurotransmitters, collagen and melanin. However, its redox activity requires tight homeostatic control. The P-type ATPases ATP7A and ATP7B help deliver copper to cuproenzymes, and ATP7B mediates the excretion of excess copper into bile. Pathogenic ATP7B variants cause Wilson disease (WD), leading to copper accumulation in organs including the liver, kidney, and brain, and to disruption of copper-dependent processes. Current treatments primarily reduce systemic copper levels, while emerging gene therapies aim to restore ATP7B function. A complementary therapeutic strategy would be to rescue dysfunctional ATP7B using pharmacological chaperones, but their development is limited by an insufficient understanding of how WD variants perturb ATP7B structure and function. Here, we present a cryo-EM structure of human ATP7B reconstituted in lipid nanodiscs together with coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations, as well as mutagenesis, functional and sequence analyses. We identify a salt bridge (E754-R969), crucial for the transition between inward- and outward-facing conformations, which is abolished by the R969Q disease variant. Additionally, we find a conserved stabilizing cholesterol-binding site severely disrupted by the WD variant W939C. Furthermore, we present new insights into the dynamics of metal binding domains 5 and 6 hinting at a copper relay mechanism in ATP7B. Together, these findings reveal lipid- and domain-mediated mechanisms of ATP7B regulation and explain how specific WD variants disrupt them, providing a structural framework for mutation-directed therapeutic strategies, including pharmacological chaperones.

title: A Tailor-Made Guanidine Ionizable Lipid as a Bifunctional mRNA Carrier and Nitric Oxide Production Inhibitor
abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are the leading clinical platform for mRNA delivery, yet their capacity to trigger macrophage-driven inflammatory responses remains a fundamental barrier to therapeutic safety and efficacy. Here, we introduce a design principle in which a tailor-made nitric oxide (NO) inhibitory motif is embedded directly into the ionizable lipid, creating a single molecular scaffold that simultaneously delivers mRNA and suppresses macrophage inflammation.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Resolving heterogeneous chromium redox kinetics in complex matrices via physics-informed XRF and vis-NIR spectrometry
abstract: In situ characterization of chromium (Cr) redox kinetics in heterogeneous mine tailing is often limited by spectral overlaps and matrix-dependent signal interference. While machine learning provides a tool for spectral deconvolution, empirical models frequently yield results that are inconsistent with physical laws when applied to complex geochemical matrices. This study presents a physics-informed learning framework, KI-BLS-Net, which integrates X-ray fluorescence and vis-NIR spectroscopy with theoretical rate limits derived from density functional theory and mass-action laws.

title: Artificial intelligence in basic and translational cardiovascular research
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in cardiovascular research where conventional analysis struggles with scale, heterogeneity, and multimodal integration. Its contribution differs across imaging, computational omics, mechanistic simulation, and drug discovery. This narrative review examines substantive applications of machine learning and deep learning while distinguishing them from routine bioinformatics and purely biophysical modeling. We assess independent biological units, validation strategies, and strength of inference in representative studies.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Generating Drug-like Molecules: A Taxonomy of Methods and Evaluation Strategies
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used for de novo small-molecule design, but the practical and translational utility of generated candidates depends on the configuration of the entire discovery workflow rather than on generative model architecture alone. This review adopts a workflow-based perspective on generative molecular design, tracing the process from existing molecular data sets, preprocessing and representation, to molecule generation, conditioning, candidate prioritization, evaluation, and iterative refinement.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Single-Crystal Growth, Structure, and Physical Properties of Yb2MoO6
abstract: Rare-earth molybdates are functional oxides of considerable interest because their structural and chemical flexibility enables diverse magnetic, electronic, and optical behavior. Here, millimeter-sized single crystals of $Yb_2MoO_6$ are synthesized, their crystal structure determined and physical properties investigated. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction confirms the formation of $Yb_2MoO_6$ and yielded lattice parameters of $a = 16.228(2)$ $\mathring{A}$, $b = 10.901(3)$ $\mathring{A}$, and $c = 5.286(2)$ $\mathring{A}$, in good agreement with previously reported neutron powder diffraction data. Scanning electron microscopy and energy-dispersive spectroscopy show a Yb:Mo ratio close to the expected 2:1 stoichiometry. Optical measurements based on diffuse-reflectance spectra and Tauc analysis yield an estimated optical gap of $\sim 3.28$ eV under the direct-allowed transition assumption. Magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal Curie-Weiss-like paramagnetic behavior, with an effective magnetic moment of $μ_{\mathrm{eff}} \approx 4.2μ_B$ per Yb and an apparent Weiss temperature of $θ\approx -65.7$ K, consistent with possible antiferromagnetic interactions or correlations, with no clear magnetic-ordering transition observed down to 10 K. These results establish the growth of $Yb_2MoO_6$ single crystals and provide initial insight into their structural, optical, and magnetic properties.

title: From Physics-Informed Deep Learning to Experimental Realization: Unlocking Entropy-Stabilized Titanium Halide Solid Electrolytes
abstract: Accelerating the discovery of high-performance solid electrolytes (SEs) is hindered by scarce experimental data and vast inorganic chemical spaces. Here, we present a physics-informed deep learning platform that integrates a physics-informed neural network with a dual-source graph neural network. By embedding fundamental physical constraints (e.g., lattice stability and coulombic interactions) into the training process, our framework overcomes the small-data dilemma, enabling the reliable screening of over 2 80 000 inorganic crystals.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Precision Nutrition: From Multi-Omics Integration to Personalized Dietary Interventions
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being investigated as a tool for precision nutrition because it can analyse heterogeneous dietary, clinical, physiological, behavioural, and molecular data. This narrative review critically examines how machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, natural language processing, explainable AI, continuous glucose monitoring, wearable technologies, and multi-omics approaches may support individualized nutritional assessment and decision-making.

title: Stereodivergent γ-Propargylation of α,β-Unsaturated Aldehydes
abstract: Notwithstanding tremendous progress in stereodivergent cooperative catalysis during the past decade, the application of this strategy involving propargylic substitution reaction is scarce. We report herein the first stereodivergent γ-propargylation of α,β-unsaturated aldehydes. With racemic propargylic acetates as the electrophile, this reaction is catalyzed cooperatively by a Cu(I)/Pybox or Cu(I)/phosphine complex and diphenylprolinol silyl ether to deliver γ-propargylic α,β-unsaturated aldehydes, bearing two adjacent stereocenters, with complete regio- (γ- over α-) and (E)-selectivity as…
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: De Novo Folding Mechanisms of Lasso Peptides
abstract: Lasso peptides adopt a distinctive [1] rotaxane conformation, yet the principles governing the folding of this kinetically trapped structure have remained elusive. Here, we integrated extensive molecular dynamics simulations and deep learning to elucidate the de novo folding mechanism of 20 lasso peptides lacking secondary post-translational modifications. We constructed Multi-Ensemble Markov Models for each lasso peptide and uncovered a consistent uphill folding landscape with spontaneous folding probabilities below 0.8%. Loop stability strongly correlated with folding propensity.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Large Single Crystal Growth and Transport Properties of KCd$_4$As$_3$ and RbCd$_4$As$_3$
abstract: Large-size KCd$_4$As$_3$ and RbCd$_4$As$_3$ single crystals were grown using the flux method. Appropriate flux for growing single crystals was determined to be Cd$_2$As, resulting in the increase in their size to be a centimeter for KCd$_4$As$_3$. The KCd$_4$As$_3$ and RbCd$_4$As$_3$ crystals exhibited metal-like temperature dependences of their electrical resistivities with negative Seebeck coefficients, characterizing them as n-type thermoelectric materials.

title: A Deep Operator Network to Predict Thermal Dose on Brain Tumors in MRI-Guided Laser Induced Thermal Therapy: with Synthetic Data
abstract: Background: MRI-guided laser interstitial thermal therapy (LITT) provides minimally invasive option for surgical treatment of recurrent brain tumors. While patient-specific prediction of thermal dose distributions would improve treatment planning, no quantitative methods currently exist for this purpose. Although conventional numerical solvers are being widely investigated, these methods are computationally expensive and often limited by accuracy and reliability. Purpose: Here we propose DeepoLITT, a rapid and accurate model to predict quantitatively heat propagation in LITT procedures.

title: Water purification method turns old batteries into magnetic pollutant traps
abstract: How can harmful substances be removed from water? When it comes to dyes that cannot simply be filtered out, this is usually very laborious: You need substances to which the dyes attach, and then the water often has to be painstakingly centrifuged.

title: N–Atom Transfer Reactivity of Terminal Cobalt Nitrides
abstract: We report the photogeneration and characterization of four-coordinate terminal cobalt nitrides (EmL)Co(N)(L) (L = pyridine, 4-dimethylaminopyridine) using a sterically encumbered dipyrrin ligand environment. The photolytic generation of the terminal nitride complexes were achieved in both the crystalline state and in frozen solution matrices to determine its molecular (single-crystal X-ray diffraction) and electronic structures (EPR).
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Advancing MEMS Gas Sensors Through Intelligent Sensing Architectures and Stability Enhancement Strategies
abstract: The growing demand for real-time chemical monitoring has accelerated the development of micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS) gas sensors as compact, low-power, and highly integrable sensing platforms. While remarkable progress in materials engineering and device miniaturization has enabled substantial improvements in sensing performance, challenges associated with gas selectivity, signal drift, and operational stability remain major barriers to real-world deployment.

title: Asymmetric NIR-II Voltage-Sensitive Dyes Enable Through-Skull Single-Cell Voltage Recordings of Neurons
abstract: Optical measurements of neuronal membrane voltage in vivo are limited by light scattering at visible wavelengths. Fluorophores operating in the second near-infrared window (NIR-II) offer improved tissue penetration; however, the reported NIR-II dyes generally lack voltage sensitivity because their dynamic symmetric structures disfavor field-sensitive charge separation. Here, we report a chemically optimized family of asymmetric NIR-II voltage-sensitive dyes.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Mesoporous Defect-Assisted Ce-Doped Cu-SSZ-13 Enabling Low-Temperature NH3–SCR via Enhanced Oxygen Transfer
abstract: Coupling efficient redox cycling with molecular diffusion in confined microporous environments remains a central challenge in zeolite catalysis. In Cu-exchanged SSZ-13 catalysts for NH3-assisted NOx reduction, low-temperature activity is limited by sluggish Cu redox interconversion and mass-transport constraints, while incorporation of secondary cations often intensifies pore-diffusion penalties. Herein, we show that defect-mediated mesostructuring enables the stable incorporation of atomically dispersed Ce species within Cu-SSZ-13, forming a Cu–Ce adjacent structure that synergistically modulates transport and redox chemistry. In situ spectroscopic and isotope-labeling analyses combined with multiscale simulations reveal that the engineered defect network enhances NOx and NH3 diffusion, while Ce species anchored at defect-edge sites promote oxygen activation and accelerate Cu-NO2 intermediate formation. These effects collectively facilitate more efficient Cu2+/Cu+ cycling across a substantially broadened temperature window. The resulting catalyst achieves ≥90% NOx conversion between 147 and 560 °C. More broadly, this work establishes defect-enabled secondary-cation stabilization as a promising strategy to decouple diffusion limitations from redox optimization in confined catalytic systems.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Iodine(III)-Enabled Photocatalytic Skeletal Editing of Carbocyclic Amides Via Radical–Polar Crossover
abstract: Skeletal editing enables the direct modification of molecular frameworks through atom insertion, deletion, or replacement. However, catalytic nitrogen insertion into ring-strained C–C bonds remains challenging, particularly for the synthesis of saturated diazacycles from readily available carbocyclic precursors. Here, we report an iodine(III)-enabled photocatalytic strategy for the skeletal editing of carbocyclic amides through a radical–polar crossover pathway.

title: Science is the bitter lesson AI hasn’t learned yet
abstract: Researchers must develop and demand tools able to look beyond what is already known

title: Multi-spectral virtual staining for label-free histopathology using deep neural networks
abstract: Virtual staining (VS) has gained a significant interest for label-free characterization of unstained tissue-sections. The concept of VS lies on translating a label-free imaging technique such as auto-fluorescence for generating an equivalent histologically stained image using deep-neural-networks. Different endogenous fluorophores present in the sample have distinct excitation and emission bands, which can provide stain-free specificity of molecules. However, conventional technique for studying emission of different molecules, restrict molecular specificity in the measurements.

title: Transfer learning across the EC classification hierarchy overcomes data scarcity in drug-target interaction prediction
abstract: Predicting drug-target interactions (DTIs) with deep learning offers opportunities to accelerate drug discovery, yet performance is often constrained by the scarcity of target-specific training data. Transfer learning relieves this limitation but requires choosing a relevant source task, a choice usually made ad hoc. Here we use the Enzyme Commission (EC) classification hierarchy as a systematic criterion for source selection, ascending the EC tree from the target enzyme until a related family carries sufficient ChEMBL bioactivity data to pre-train a deep feedforward network, which is then…

title: Toward Standardized Fucoidan Extractions from Brown Algae: Optimization of Under-Addressed Parameters to Maximize Yield and Purity
abstract: Brown algal cell walls contain unique polysaccharides called fucoidans, which exhibit complex structural diversity and have applications across a range of industries. For these applications, fucoidan extraction methods should maximize yield while minimizing co-extracted impurities. However, extraction protocols vary widely, and their effects on yield and purity are rarely investigated. Thus, standardized and optimized fucoidan extraction methods are needed. Here, we aimed to identify optimal parameters for selected steps of a fucoidan extraction protocol. Starting with a commonly used protocol, we experimentally investigated three steps critical to yield and purity: (1) alcohol-insoluble residue preparation, (2) alginate removal, and (3) ion removal by dialysis. Our results show that sequential washes with 70% and 100% ethanol removed proteins, lipids, polyphenols, and pigments during alcohol-insoluble residue preparation without sacrificing fucoidan yield.
